abstract: Background Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18-45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores. Results Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05-7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β -0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β -0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores. Conclusions FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.

abstract: This exploratory pilot study asked whether frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) recorded while a price is displayed varies with the satisfaction-rating change a consumer then makes. Twenty-one participants completed two blocks of 30 trials: view a product, give a pre-price rating (1-9), see the price, give a post-price rating, which they were instructed to change except at the scale limits. The change is described by its direction and magnitude (|Δ|, provisionally labeled Decision Momentum), two descriptions of one difference score. FAA was computed from relative alpha power at F3/F4 over 0-3 s after price onset on average-referenced data. Inference rests on 19 participants and 820 trials. The primary pooled test of the direction × magnitude interaction was inconclusive (β=-0.051, 95% CI [-0.111,0.009], p = 0.093). An exploratory block-stratified analysis found an interaction in the first block (β=-0.087, 95% CI [-0.152,-0.021], p = 0.010), although neither of its two component slopes differed clearly from zero. Support varied across specifications, and five alternative operationalizations of FAA did not reproduce it. The same model applied to the window before price onset, where the predictors cannot yet reflect the price, produced an interaction of comparable or larger size pooled and in the second block. In the first block, the direct comparison did not establish a difference between windows, and adjusting for pre-price FAA left the first-block estimate unchanged (p = 0.008); in the second block, the two windows did differ (p = 0.021), the association being present before the price and not after it. Single-trial classification of change direction showed modest performance with uncertain generalizability (ROC AUC 0.538; participant bootstrap 95% CI [0.476, 0.564]). The association is reported as hypothesis-generating; attributing it specifically to price-related processing is not supported by these data.

abstract: Gut symbionts condition mucosal immunity to resist infection by enteropathogens, but the specific microbes and mechanisms involved differ significantly between host species. In higher primates, bacterial metabolite HMB-PP is sensed by a specialized population of Vγ9Vδ2+T-cells, which we now report can potently suppress growth of endogenous fungi in human intestinal organ cultures. In healthy intestine, HMB-PP-stimulated Vδ2+ T-cells restricted outgrowth of keystone fungus Candida albicans via a mechanism that required IL-22. In Crohn's disease (CD), Vδ2+ T-cells were poorly responsive to HMB-PP and permitted outgrowth of C. albicans strains that formed toxin-producing filaments, triggered neutrophil extracellular traps, and induced macrophage IL-1β release ex vivo. Genomic and proteomic analysis of the Candida isolates suggested increased tissue adhesion of CD-derived strains, which rapidly invaded the gut barrier in an 'intestine-on-a-chip' model. These data reveal that bacterial activation of Vδ2+ T-cells suppresses fungal pathobionts in human gut via an IL-22-dependent mechanism that is dysregulated in CD.

abstract: Background 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach. Methods IPF-related genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis combining differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate targets were obtained by intersecting IPF-associated genes with predicted 5-HMF targets. Functional enrichment analysis, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP interpretation were performed to prioritize candidate targets, while molecular docking was used to explore potential 5-HMF-target interactions. A bleomycin-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was further used to evaluate the effects of 5-HMF on fibrotic lung injury and the transcriptional expression of prioritized candidate genes. Results A total of 1,776 IPF-associated genes and 143 predicted 5-HMF targets were identified, yielding 12 overlapping candidate targets. Enrichment analysis implicated these genes in fibrosis-related pathways, including chemical carcinogenesis-receptor activation and estrogen signaling. Machine learning analysis prioritized seven core targets (CA2, CA4, ESR2, F10, HSP90AA1, PLA2G1B, and PTPRB), all of which accommodated 5-HMF in their orthosteric pockets in blind docking, albeit with weak, non-selective Vina scores (-4.5 to -5.4 kcal/mol). In vivo, 5-HMF significantly exacerbated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, as demonstrated by aggravated lung injury, increased collagen deposition, and elevated expression of Hsp90aa1, Pla2g1b, Ca4, F10, Acta2, and Col1a1. Conclusion Our findings suggest that 5-HMF may exacerbate fibrotic lung injury through multiple fibrosis-related molecular targets and pathways. These findings provide preliminary evidence for a potential association between 5-HMF exposure and the aggravation of pulmonary fibrosis, while further studies are required to determine whether 5-HMF can independently initiate fibrotic pathology.

title: Juggling skill acquisition through air-toss and ground-bounce practice in college students: A study protocol for the TuJuggling cluster-randomised trial.

abstract: Introduction Practice organization is vital for motor acquisition, yet pragmatic evidence on how instructional constraints shape learning in authentic settings remains scarce. The TuJuggling protocol establishes a standardised assessment and training framework for complex bimanual skills in novices using an ecological dynamics perspective. Methods In this cluster-randomised crossover trial, registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07528924), 200 students will complete two 4-week juggling interventions: air-toss (A) and floor-rebound (B), separated by a 1-week washout. The primary outcome is a Global Composite Score (40 tasks) across stable (floor) and unstable (BOSU) surfaces. Secondary outcomes include cognitive functions (attentional/inhibitory control, visuospatial memory, and working memory), handgrip strength, and psychological factors (flow and affect). Assessments occur at baseline and after each intervention period. Results Data will be analysed using linear mixed models (LMM) to evaluate the effects of method, period, and sequence while accounting for the cluster-based design. Missing data will be handled via Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML). Mediation models will further investigate whether psycho-cognitive shifts explain the observed motor training effects. Discussion This protocol provides a rigorous framework to evaluate how physical constraints and exposure order shape coordination. Findings will offer evidence-based recommendations for sequencing motor skill progressions in higher education, bridging theoretical motor learning and applied pedagogy.

abstract: Background Drug overdose is a leading cause of death among people released from correctional facilities, and the risk of overdose is higher among people living with HIV (PLWH). Overdose remains understudied in people in South Africa despite the high burden of HIV and hazardous opioid use. The researchers aimed to qualitatively explore how formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and OUD in South Africa understand, experience, and respond to overdose. Methods People with HIV and self-reported hazardous opioid use prior to correctional facility release or shortly after release were enrolled in a convenience sample. Twenty-three formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and opioid use in or around Tshwane, South Africa completed sequential in-depth interviews that explored medication-assisted treatment for hazardous opioid use and HIV care delivery. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using both deductive and inductive coding, with a focus on participants' knowledge and definition of overdose, personal experiences with overdose, and responses to overdose. Results All participants used the term "overdose", but there was no unified understanding of what constitutes an overdose or how to manage an overdose. The period immediately following release from incarceration was identified as a key moment in which overdose occurred. Pouring water onto the person overdosing was reported to be the most prevalent response strategy. Only two participants contacted or watched their peers contact the ambulance. Fear of law enforcement involvement was perceived as a barrier to calling for emergency services. Conclusion The findings identify a gap in overdose knowledge among corrections-involved people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa. There is a need to increase knowledge regarding overdose recognition and responses.

title: LEM-3/ANKLE1 nuclease prevents the formation of abnormal syncytium to safeguard neuronal differentiation.

author_details.name: Deng S
author_details.affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China.

author_details.name: Zheng C
author_details.affiliation: School of Biological Sciences, The University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China.

abstract: In animal development, cells exit the cell cycle after a final round of cell division to differentiate into specialized cell types. However, the impact of failed cytokinesis on the fate specification of postmitotic cells, especially neurons, remains poorly understood. We analyzed the Caenorhabditis elegans mutants lacking the midbody-tethered endonuclease LEM-3/ANKLE1, which resolves chromatin bridges during cytokinesis. Using genetic analysis, fluorescence microscopy, and RNA visualization, we found that unresolved DNA bridges lead to the formation of stable intercellular bridges, creating binucleate syncytia between touch receptor neurons and sister cells, which allows thorough cytoplasmic mixing despite independent nuclear transcription. In some cases, the cytoplasmic linkage between sister cells also led to the suppression of neuronal fates and prevention of apoptotic fates. Thus, LEM-3 prevents syncytium formation to ensure proper cellular differentiation.

title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

author_details.name: Lv H
author_details.affiliation: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan, China.

author_details.name: Gao Y

author_details.name: Yu A
author_details.affiliation: Department of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, West China Hospital, Sichuan University, Chengdu, Sichuan, China.

abstract: Background Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study. Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. Conclusion In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

title: Machine learning-based thermoelectric materials screening with physical consistency and uncertainty propagation.

author_details.name: Ahmad A
author_details.affiliation: Research Center for Eco-environmental Engineering, School of Environment and Civil Engineering, Dongguan University of Technology, Dongguan, China.

abstract: Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising strategy for accelerating thermoelectric materials discovery. However, direct prediction of the thermoelectric figure of merit (ZT) often can introduce target leakage and overestimates predictive performance because ZT is intrinsically derived from multiple transport properties. In this work, a physics-guided and uncertainty-aware ML framework is developed for thermoelectric material screening by independently predicting the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity, and thermal conductivity, followed by analytical evaluation of thermoelectric performance. Experimental data from the ESTM database were evaluated using material-wise validation, with exact chemical formulas kept exclusively in either the training or held-out test subset to reduce material-level information leakage. Predictive uncertainty was quantified using ensemble learning and propagated into thermoelectric performance evaluation and uncertainty-aware LCB screening. The proposed framework demonstrates strong predictive capability for individual transport properties while providing physically consistent thermoelectric performance estimation. Although the framework exhibits lower apparent predictive accuracy than direct ZT regression models, it provides improved interpretability and a more physically structured approach to thermoelectric performance evaluation. The results demonstrate that integrating physical consistency, uncertainty propagation, and uncertainty-aware screening provides a robust strategy for data-driven thermoelectric materials screening.

abstract: Background Bryozoans are ancient colonial animals that have existed for over 470 million years and are widely distributed across aquatic environments. Recently, many spherical colloids (average diameter≈1 meter in diameter), containing bryozoans and diverse microorganisms, were found in the Hanjiang river in China. In this study, we investigated these bryozoan-dominated microbial complexes using metagenomic sequencing, metabolomic profiling, and complementary approaches. Results The results revealed that the microbial structure dominated by bryozoans included eukaryotes such as fungi, microalgae, as well as prokaryotes such as bacteria, and acellular entities such as viruses. All members form a highly integrated consortium that collaboratively maintains community function and stability, which displayed the shape and structure of a regular microbial complex and increased in size. Additionally, the results suggested the predominately presence of Proteobacteria were particularly abundant and are known to produce bryozoans in response to bryozoan signals. Interesting, it was implied that a decrease or even a loss in virulence occurs when pathogenic microorganisms become members of the complex. This is the first study focusing on the composition and metabolites of the unusual microorganism complex. The results discovered the close and intriguing connections within the microbial communities dominated by the ancient organism bryozoan through multi-omics technologies. It showed that both eukaryotes and prokaryotes can coordinate, thereby forming a stable composite structure.

title: Museum visitors' acceptance of digital services in China and Russia: Extending UTAUT2 with individual-level cultural values.

author_details.name: Chen J
author_details.affiliation: College of Landscape Architecture and Arts, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, Shaanxi, China.; Institute of Philosophy, St Petersburg University, St Petersburg, Russia.

author_details.name: Li X

abstract: Museum digital services have become an important means of supporting visitors' access to information, understanding of exhibition content, and broader museum experiences. However, the mechanisms underlying visitors' acceptance of these services may vary across visitor groups. Drawing on a context-adapted Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology model (UTAUT2), this study incorporates three individual-level cultural values-collectivism orientation, uncertainty avoidance, and long-term orientation-to examine acceptance intention toward museum digital services in China and Russia. The model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with survey data from China (n = 316) and Russia (n = 307). Measurement invariance of composites (MICOM) and PLS multigroup analysis (PLS-MGA) were conducted to assess between-sample differences. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and hedonic motivation all had significant positive effects on acceptance intention in both samples. The PLS-MGA results showed no significant between-sample differences in the effects of performance expectancy or social influence. Hedonic motivation had a significantly stronger effect in the Chinese sample, whereas effort expectancy and facilitating conditions had stronger effects in the Russian sample. The latter two differences should nevertheless be interpreted cautiously because compositional invariance was not established for these constructs. Collectivism strengthened the effect of social influence, uncertainty avoidance strengthened the effects of effort expectancy and facilitating conditions, and long-term orientation strengthened the effects of performance expectancy and hedonic motivation. None of the five moderating effects differed significantly between the two samples. These findings show that acceptance intention toward museum digital services is jointly shaped by functional benefits, ease of use, social cues, available support, experiential value, and visitors' individual cultural value orientations. The study provides evidence of both shared acceptance mechanisms and sample-specific path differences and offers a basis for visitor segmentation and the refinement of museum digital services.

abstract: Objective This study aimed to investigate the association of an Online Co-care Management (OCCM) model with changes in glycemic control and metabolic indicators among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Methods Based on clinical follow-up records, we conducted a retrospective cohort study with a propensity score (PS)-matched control group.The OCCM group included patients enrolled in the integrated care clinic from 2022 to 2025 (n = 406). Among patients who did not participate in OCCM (n = 199) during the study period, PS-matched controls were selected at a 1:1 ratio.The PS model included age, sex, diabetes duration, smoking, drinking, medication use, and follow-up duration.After matching, 240 patients were included in the final analysis, with 120 patients in each group. Follow-up data were collected at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. Longitudinal data on anthropometrics, glycemic indices, blood pressure, lipid profiles, and organ function were analyzedusing repeated measures ANOVA. Results Over a 6-month follow-up period, HbA1c levels decreased more markedly in the OCCM group compared with the usual-care group. In the OCCM group, HbA1c declined from 7.403 ± 1.748% at baseline to 6.591 ± 0.871% at 3 months and 6.593 ± 1.056% at 6 months, while in the usual-care group, it changed from 6.310 ± 1.277% to 6.225 ± 1.017% and 6.534 ± 1.598%, respectivelyRepeated-measures ANOVA revealed significant time, group, and time × group effects for HbA1c (F = 10.608, P < 0.001; F = 16.748, P < 0.001; F = 14.546, P < 0.001). BMI, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, and lipid profiles, also showed greater improvements in the OCCM group than in controls. Conclusion The OCCM model was associated with short-term improvements in glycemic and metabolic indicators among T2DM patients, suggesting it may be an effective approach for structured chronic disease management.

title: Pediatric emergency medicine in Lebanon: Physician-perceived comfort levels, challenges, and educational needs.

author_details.name: Moughnieh N

abstract: Background Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) is a rapidly evolving subspecialty that improves the quality and safety of care for children. Despite global advancements, PEM remains underdeveloped in many low- and middle-income countries, including Lebanon. Despite a large pediatric population there is no formal paediatric emergency medicine system in place, and care largely delivered by physicians practicing without standardized or specialized training. This lack of dedicated PEM training and organized emergency care pathways may compromise the timely recognition and management of pediatric emergencies, potentially affecting patient outcomes. Objectives The present study aimed to assess physicians perceived comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, identify training gaps, and explore systemic and institutional challenges affecting pediatric emergency care in Lebanon. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians involved in pediatric emergency care across Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed self-reported comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, perceived challenges, and priorities for training and PEM workforce development. Results Responses from 59 physicians were analysed. Most were male 38 (64.4%), with a median clinical experience of 7 years. General pediatricians represented 28 (47.5%), emergency physicians 17 (28.8%), PEM specialists 8 (13.6%), and pediatric intensivists 6 (10.2%). Physicians reported high perceived comfort in pediatric fluid management 52(88.1%), chest X-ray interpretation 46 (77.9%), and general pediatric emergencies 42 (71.2%), but lower comfort in procedural sedation, suturing 35 (59.6%), fracture stabilization 35 (59.4%), and Extended Focused Assessment Sonography in Trauma (EFAST) 22 (41.8%). General pediatricians reported greater comfort with general pediatric emergencies, while emergency-focused physicians had higher comfort with trauma-related skills and procedural interventions. Major challenges included gaps in practical and theoretical training, limited hospital infrastructure, shortages of devices and human resources, and the need for continuing medical education. Nearly all participants 57 (96.6%) supported the establishing a dedicated PEM fellowship, highlighting training priorities in trauma, medical emergencies, life support, procedural skills, and pediatric imaging. Conclusion Pediatric emergency care in Lebanon is constrained by gaps in skills, training, and systemic resources. There is an urgent need to establish standardized PEM training pathways, enhance curricula, and strengthen system-level preparedness. Implementing these measures will support a competent PEM workforce and improve the quality and safety of emergency care for children nationwide.

abstract: Student retention intention remains a concern for higher education systems worldwide and is relevant to institutional sustainability and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Human Capital Theory (HCT) and Expectancy-Value Theory (EVT), this study examines the direct and indirect associations between perceived quality teaching and student retention intention through students' self-reported knowledge, skills, competencies and student loyalty. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 395 final-year students across Pakistani universities using a multistage sampling approach, with institutions selected through stratified random sampling and participants recruited via convenience sampling. The proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that perceived quality teaching is positively associated with student retention intention, both directly and indirectly through students' knowledge, skills, and competencies and student loyalty. Significant indirect associations were identified through each mediator separately and through the proposed serial mediation pathway. These findings highlight the relevance of considering students' perceived capability development and institutional attachment together when examining retention intention. HCT provides a rationale for the relationship between perceived teaching quality and students' knowledge, skills, competencies, while EVT offers an interpretive perspective; however, expectancy of success and subjective task value were not directly measured. The cross-sectional design also precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. Practically, the findings suggest that faculty development, student-centered pedagogies, digitally supported teaching, and curriculum alignment with labor market needs merit consideration in institutional quality assurance. The findings provide context-specific evidence from Pakistani higher education (HE) and are relevant to SDG 4 through their focus on perceived teaching quality and students' intentions to continue their studies. They do not establish effects on actual retention or broader educational outcomes.

abstract: Objective This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and willingness of psychiatrists to promote long-acting injectable antipsychotics (LAIs) in Fujian Province, China, and to identify the influencing factors. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted using convenience sampling among psychiatrists attending a provincial conference. An 18-item online questionnaire was distributed via Wenjuanxing. Descriptive statistics, Mann-Whitney U tests and Spearman's rank correlation were used. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied for multiple correlations. Results A total of 222 psychiatrists completed the survey, with 90 respondents (40.5%) identifying as female. The largest age group was 30-39 years (46.9%). Most participants (51.4%) had > 10 years of clinical experience, and 65 (29.3%) held senior professional titles. Most participants reported adequate knowledge of LAIs (96.4%), recognized their therapeutic value (80.2%) and favorable application prospects (87.8%), and expressed a willingness to promote LAIs (82.4%).High cost was identified as the primary barrier to clinical use (90.5%) and the most critical factor for wider adoption (88.3%). Psychiatrists with more clinical experience (>10 years) held significantly more positive attitudes regarding overall therapeutic value, willingness to promote LAIs, and support for early application (all P < 0.05). Spearman's correlation analysis indicated that positive attitudes were significantly associated with greater clinical experience (ρ = 0.302, q < 0.01) and higher levels of knowledge (ρ = 0.297, q < 0.01) after FDR correction. Conclusion Psychiatrists in Fujian Province demonstrated adequate knowledge and generally positive attitudes toward LAIs. Psychiatrists' willingness to promote LAIs was associated with knowledge level and clinical experience, but reducing the cost of drug patents may contribute to improving the prescription rates. Future efforts should focus on systematic training, academic communication, positive prescribing experiences, and policy coordination to overcome cost and stigma barriers.

abstract: As an innovative multiple access technology, hybrid power-frequency multiple access (HPMA) effectively supports massive connectivity while eliminating the decoding complexity associated with successive interference cancellation (SIC). Concurrently, although the keyhole effect represents a critical propagation degradation that drastically reduces diversity gains in wireless channels, its impact on advanced multiple-access techniques remains largely explored. Driven by these considerations, this paper investigates a comprehensive performance evaluation of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-assisted HPMA framework deployed over keyhole Nakagami-m fading environments. Specifically, exact closed-form formulations of outage probability (OP), ergodic capacity (EC), and average bit error rate (ABER) are derived, supplemented by high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) asymptotic expansions to yield deeper engineering insights. Monte Carlo simulations verify the exactness of the theoretical analysis and demonstrate the resilience of the proposed HPMA system under realistic keyhole fading scenarios. Our findings reveal that HPMA maintains high performance under severe keyhole conditions, attaining substantial performance superiorities over standard non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), particularly regarding outage behavior and error rates. Finally, this study highlights HPMA as a promising, low-complexity, and resource-efficient radio access technology for next-generation wireless communications subjected to keyhole propagation constraints.

title: Pre-service mathematics teachers' integration of design thinking in STEM lesson plans: Insights from a qualitative case study.

author_details.name: Karaman Dündar R
author_details.affiliation: Department of Mathematics and Science Education, Bartin University, Bartin, Türkiye.

abstract: Mathematics is foundational in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. Mathematics can foster problem-solving, quantitative reasoning, modeling, and creativity across disciplines. This study explores how pre-service mathematics teachers (PMTs) in a Design Thinking (DT)-focused course integrate DT into STEM lesson planning, the factors influencing this integration, and the challenges encountered during lesson planning. 55 senior PMTs at a state university in Türkiye participated in the study. Data were collected through DT-oriented, mathematics-focused STEM lesson plans and an open-ended questionnaire and were analyzed using content analysis. Findings reveal that while many PMTs maintained mathematics as a core component in their plans, the integration of DT was often partial and unbalanced. The Define, Ideate, and Prototype phases were predominant across most plans (>80%), whereas the Empathy phase was considerably less represented, appearing in only 20.8% of plans. In contrast, while the Test phase was incorporated into more than half of the lesson plans (54.2%), its presence remained substantially lower than that of the initial construction phases, reflecting a tendency toward linear product completion rather than sustained, iterative design optimization. Participants reported difficulties aligning DT phases with learning objectives, selecting appropriate materials, and designing effective assessment strategies. Despite these challenges, PMTs strongly believed in DT's potential to enhance student engagement, creativity, and real-world mathematical thinking. The study underscores the need for teacher education programs to provide more explicit scaffolding and practical tools to meaningfully embed all phases of DT within mathematics instruction.

abstract: Background Blood pressure(BP) control remains suboptimal worldwide. Sex-related disparities in hypertension have been reported, but data from South Asia are limited. Understanding the epidemiology and sex-related differences is essential to improve BP control. Objectives To assess the prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension among Sri Lankans. Methods We analysed secondary data from the Sri Lanka STEPS Survey 2021, a nationally representative, community-based, cross-sectional study. Hypertension was defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive use; controlled BP as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Prevalences, associations, and sex-related disparities in hypertension, undiagnosed hypertension, and BP control were assessed using logistic regression. Results Data from 4,634 adults(mean age 43.5(weighted CI 43.0-44.1) years; female 54.8 (53.1-56.5)%) were analysed. Overall, 37.2(35.5-38.9)% had hypertension, of whom 60.0(58.1-63.4) % were previously undiagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 73.6 (73.6, 69.6-77.2)% were on treatment, but only 38.0(33.0-44.20)% achieved BP targets. The rates of hypertension prevalence (p = 0.600), treated hypertension (p = 0.398), and controlled blood pressure (p = 0.819) in females and males did not differ significantly by sex. However, undiagnosed hypertension was significantly higher in males (69.4%, 65.3-73.1) than in females (53.6%, 50.1-57.0) (p < 0.001). Differences in the associations of hypertension by sex were noted; diabetes was associated only in females (p < 0.001), while wealth quintile (p < 0.001) and 24-hour urinary salt excretion (p = 0.011) were associated only in males. Overweight/obesity was shown to have a significant association with undiagnosed hypertension only in males (p = 0.017) in stratified analyses. Conclusions More than half of the hypertensives in this South Asian population were previously undiagnosed. Of hypertensives, ¾ were treated, but only 1/3 achieved treatment goals. Prevalence, treatment and control rates of hypertension were not different between females and males, but undiagnosed hypertension was more common in men. Therefore, the emphasis should be on improving the detection of hypertension, especially in men, and on treating to targets in both sexes.

title: Prognostic value of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in glioma: A meta-analysis.

abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate the predictive value of systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) for the prognosis of glioma patients. Methods PubMed, Cochrane Library, EMBASE, and Web of Science databases were searched to collect literature on the relationship between SIRI and glioma prognosis from database inception to July 2026. The primary outcome measures were overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). STATA 15.0 and Review Manager 5.4 software were used, and random-effects models were employed with pooled hazard ratios (HR) and their 95% confidence intervals (CI) to assess the prognostic value of SIRI. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed. Results Eight retrospective cohort studies involving 1778 glioma patients were included, forming 12 comparison groups for OS analysis and 4 comparison groups for PFS analysis. Meta-analysis results showed that a higher SIRI was significantly associated with poorer OS (pooled HR = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.34-2.38, P < 0.0001) and PFS (pooled HR = 1.46, 95% CI: 1.18-1.81, P = 0.0005) in glioma patients. Subgroup analysis showed that the prognostic value of SIRI for OS was not significant in the European population subgroup, suggesting that the association may be modulated by geographic region. Sensitivity analysis confirmed the robustness of the results. Egger's test indicated publication bias in the OS analysis (P = 0.0001), but no significant bias was found in the PFS analysis. Conclusion This meta-analysis suggests that elevated SIRI is associated with poorer OS and PFS in glioma patients, although this association was not consistently observed across all subgroups, particularly in European populations. These findings highlight the need for further validation with standardized cut-off values in diverse populations.

abstract: Against the macro backdrop of the strategy for developing a strong sporting nation and digital-intelligent transformation, sports organizations have accumulated massive high-value unstructured knowledge assets such as academic literature and reports. Yet their latent strategic value has not been effectively exploited. Converting static knowledge assets into dynamic strategic intelligence represents the central challenge in sports knowledge management.Taking 169 high quality journal papers on gymnastics published from 2016 to 2025 in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI, domestic edition) as research objects, this study identifies seven Topics using the Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) model: Topic 1: Technical analysis of bar transitions and choreography in gymnastics competitions; Topic 2: Evolution of the global team structure in men's artistic gymnastics; Topic 3: Biomechanical analysis of landing techniques among gymnasts; Topic 4: Research on curriculum design and instructional practice in school gymnastics education; Topic 5: Research on balance capability in 'gymnasts' apparatus performances; Topic 6: Movement technique analysis of elite gymnasts; Topic 7: Talent cultivation for reserve forces in competitive gymnastics. Quantitative Topic evaluation shows that Topic 4 is a high-concentration and high-coverage Topic; Topic 5 and 6 are high-concentration and low-coverage Topics; Topic 1 is a low-concentration and low-coverage Topic; and Topic 2, 3, and 7 are low-concentration and high-coverage Topics. This study conducts a Topic-based four-quadrant classification diagnosis and proposes differentiated development paths. Accordingly, it identifies future research directions for Topics in each quadrant, including theoretical deepening, application expansion, basic cultivation, and knowledge integration.

title: Recurrent enhancer-promoter interactions across samples.

author_details.name: Weston M
author_details.affiliation: Department of Computer Science, University of Central Florida, Orlando, Florida, United States of America.

author_details.affiliation: Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, University of Central Florida, Orlando, Florida, United States of America.

author_details.affiliation: Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, College of Medicine, University of Central Florida, Orlando, Florida, United States of America.

abstract: Enhancer-promoter interactions (EPIs) are fundamental to gene regulation, and clarifying their recurrence across diverse biological contexts is key to understanding chromatin architecture. Here, we systematically evaluate EPI recurrence using 95 HiChIP and 266 Hi-C datasets spanning multiple cell types, cell lines, and experimental conditions. We find that each of the majority of EPIs identified in any given sample is also observed in other samples, largely independent of assay type, cellular context, or enhancer annotation strategy. EPIs unique to an individual sample tend to occur in regions with fewer neighboring EPIs or in a sample with greater sequencing depth, indicating that many such "unique" EPIs likely reflect low sequencing depth rather than true biological specificity. Collectively, our results suggest that most human EPIs may have already been cataloged, and that gene regulation primarily relies on the selective reuse of a shared pool of EPIs across contexts. Thus, while EPIs are context-specific in pairwise sample comparisons, they are broadly recurrent when considered across a large compendium of samples. These findings underscore the pervasive and reusable nature of EPIs and have important implications for the interpretation of chromatin conformation data.

title: Residual-activated smooth sliding-mode control for actuator-limited quadrotor UAV attitude-altitude tracking.

author_details.name: Le TL
author_details.affiliation: Faculty of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology and Engineering, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

author_details.name: Hsieh MF
author_details.affiliation: Department of Electrical Engineering, National Cheng Kung University, Tainan City, Taiwan.

abstract: Residual tracking errors may persist in actuator-limited quadrotors after the main transient has decayed, particularly when motor lag, dead-zone behavior, thrust saturation, rotor drag, and partial motor-effectiveness loss weaken corrective action near the sliding surface. This study develops a friction-mode residual reaching law (FRMRL) for robust attitude-altitude control of a quadrotor UAV. The law retains the smoothness of a bounded sliding-mode reaching function and adds a residual-activated term that becomes effective when the sliding variable remains nonzero while the corresponding angular or vertical rate is small. It therefore strengthens the reaching action in the low-rate residual regime without increasing switching authority across the full operating range. The controller is formulated for a cascaded quadrotor architecture in which the directly actuated attitude-altitude channels are modeled as matched-input second-order subsystems subject to lumped perturbations and actuator nonlinearities. Lyapunov analysis establishes uniform ultimate boundedness under bounded perturbations and asymptotic convergence in the nominal case; it also shows a stronger local descent rate than the smooth reaching baseline in the residual regime. FRMRL is evaluated against PID, constant-rate SMC, exponential-reaching-law SMC, adaptive SMC, and a gain-matched smooth-reaching-law ablation baseline across six scenarios: nominal tracking, matched disturbances, wind-like disturbances, parameter uncertainty, actuator saturation with dead-zone, and partial motor-effectiveness loss. FRMRL achieves the lowest study-specific journal-oriented quality score in all six scenarios. Its mean score is 13.2%, 19.7%, 49.9%, and 78.4% lower than the corresponding mean scores for ERL-SMC, ASMC, CRL-SMC, and PID, respectively. Across the six scenarios, FRMRL also yields a mean total IAE of 15.5468 and a mean peak-to-peak control ripple of 0.3783. The gain-matched ablation indicates that residual activation, rather than differences in baseline gains, accounts for the improvement in residual-error suppression and control smoothness.

abstract: Only a fraction of bacterial genomes encode CRISPR-Cas systems, but the selective causes of this variation are unexplained. How naturally virulent bacteriophages (phages) select for CRISPR immunity has rarely been tested experimentally. Here, we show against a panel of genetically and functionally diverse virulent phages that CRISPR immunity was not universally beneficial to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and its fitness effect varied strongly between phages in predictable ways. In addition to mechanisms known to alter the effectiveness of CRISPR immunity, such as encoding a matching spacer or a protective nuclear shell, we show that the fitness effect of CRISPR immunity negatively associated with the probability of evolving receptor-based resistance to the phage via spontaneous mutation. The supply of resistance mutations differed strongly between very closely related lipopolysaccharide-binding phages and was associated with variation at the C-terminus of the tail fibre protein altering residues involved in hydrogen bonding and the predicted binding site. Our results show that CRISPR immunity is more beneficial against virulent phages that are harder to evolve resistance to via receptor mutations, suggesting that virulent phage community composition and diversity will be important drivers of the prevalence of CRISPR immunity.

title: Robust optimal reinsurance and ESG investment under rating-innovation ambiguity and ESG rating uncertainty.

author_details.name: Fu J
author_details.affiliation: School of Mathematics and Statistics, Zhaotong University, Zhaotong, Yunnan, China.

abstract: ESG ratings are noisy measurements and may also be exposed to systematic credibility concerns. We study an ambiguity-averse insurer that chooses proportional reinsurance and green and brown stock positions while learning a hidden green-quality factor from stock returns and an ESG rating signal. Signal volatility represents ordinary rating uncertainty. A worst-case distortion of the rating innovation represents ambiguity about the observation model, whereas a separate out-of-model drift gtrue is used only in stress tests for systematic rating bias. This distinction prevents robust-control ambiguity from being interpreted as observed greenwashing itself. We derive the reference Kalman-Bucy filter and the separated robust control problem. Shared stock-return shocks produce a mixed wealth-belief derivative and a filtering-hedging demand. Under CARA utility, the value function is exponential-quadratic, stock feedback follows a Riccati-type system, and retention is projected onto q∈[0,1]. The verification result is conditional on explicit admissibility and integrability conditions. Primary numerical experiments with illustrative parameters identify the model mechanisms but do not constitute empirical calibration. Independent numerical checks add Monte Carlo intervals, static and insurance-only benchmarks, original-scale plots, and a 40-design parameter-uncertainty analysis. The learning-strategy intervals overlap substantially, and rating-innovation ambiguity effects are small in CE and warning probability. Tail-risk changes are more directionally consistent across the tested parameter region, but their magnitudes remain small. The numerical evidence therefore supports mechanism existence and conditional downside sensitivity, not universal or quantitatively calibrated economic relevance.

abstract: Research increasingly demonstrates that endogenous bacterial communities (microbiomes) are associated with both cognitive functioning and socioeconomic status (SES). In this study, we used a metagenomics approach to characterize oral microbiome diversity in Hispanic and African American children aged 6-16 years. We examined how microbiome composition and SES were related to cognitive performance, as assessed by the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC). Our findings indicate that SES and the microbiome contributed complementary, comparably sized influences on cognitive functioning. Together, variability in conventional SES indicators and microbiome composition accounted for approximately 10% of the variability in WISC scores. These results highlight the importance of integrating both social and biological determinants of health when studying cognitive performance and other psychological outcomes.

title: SpatioCAD: Context-aware graph diffusion model for pinpointing spatially variable genes in heterogeneous tissues.

author_details.name: Wen H

abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables comprehensive characterization of tissue architecture, and the identification of spatially variable genes (SVGs) is a critical step for defining region-specific molecular markers and uncovering spatially regulated mechanisms across diverse biological contexts. However, most existing methods for SVG detection overlook cell density variations, a major confounding factor in complex tissues such as tumors, where heterogeneous cellularity frequently introduces false-positive calls. Here we present SpatioCAD, a computational framework that explicitly decouples genuine spatial expression patterns from confounding effects driven by cellularity. SpatioCAD introduces a graph diffusion model that inherently incorporates cell-density-aware conditions to simulate expression propagation, supporting the identification of SVGs across a broad range of expression levels. Systematic evaluations on simulated datasets demonstrate its superior statistical power and specificity. Applied to breast cancer, lung cancer, and glioma datasets, SpatioCAD identifies functionally diverse SVGs, including low‑abundance transcripts with established roles in tumor progression, while also recapitulates biologically meaningful tissue architecture features. Importantly, SpatioCAD is fast and scalable to large tissues.

abstract: Existing optimization studies on large-span Suspen-Dome structures have mainly focused on either size optimization of the upper reticulated shell or topology optimization of the lower cable-strut system. Such a separated strategy prevents the integrated optimization of the whole structure, restricts the design space, and limits further improvement in structural performance. This study investigates the integrated optimization of prefabricated large-span Suspen-Dome structures by simultaneously considering the size, geometric configuration, and topology of the upper reticulated shell, together with the topology and cable forces of the lower cable-strut system. To ensure practical applicability, the design variables are classified into topological and size variables. The former define the structural configuration and connectivity, while the latter determine material-related properties. The optimization aims to maximize stiffness and minimize weight, subject to member slenderness, material strength, local stability, and overall structural stability constraints. An Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)-based candidate screening model is introduced to accelerate the optimization algorithm and reduce unnecessary ANSYS analyses. A partial full-stress design (PFSD) concept is proposed, in which the reticulated shell serves as a structural safety reserve. The proposed structural mapping method-improved plant growth algorithm (SMM-iPGSA) is validated through two examples. Results show that the optimized structures exhibit improved stability, more uniform stress distribution, and displacements well below the allowable limits.

title: Testing the theory of planned behavior in predicting evacuation intentions during storms.

author_details.name: Abukhalaf AHI

abstract: The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been widely applied to predict human behavior across diverse domains; however, its application in disaster contexts remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining the utility of TPB in predicting intentions to prepare evacuation plans in hurricane-prone areas. Using a quantitative approach, an online survey was administered to adults residing in Florida, yielding 816 valid responses. Attitude toward evacuation planning, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control were measured using validated Likert-scale items. Data were analyzed using Spearman's correlation and binary logistic regression. Results indicate that all TPB constructs were significantly associated with evacuation planning intentions. Subjective norms emerged as the strongest predictor, highlighting the critical role of social influence in preparedness decisions. Attitude toward evacuation planning and perceived behavioral control also demonstrated significant positive effects, suggesting that favorable evaluations of evacuation planning and confidence in one's ability to prepare increase preparedness intentions. The logistic regression model showed strong predictive power (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.62). These findings support the applicability of TPB in disaster preparedness research and underscore the importance of integrating social norms, perceived behavioral control, and attitude-based interventions into emergency management strategies.

title: The promiscuity and degeneracy of ten unique RNA base-pairing rules can determine the success of adaptive RNA evolution.

author_details.name: Goldbach L
author_details.affiliation: Department of Evolutionary Biology and Environmental Studies, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.; Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, Lausanne, Switzerland.

author_details.name: Martin NS
author_details.affiliation: CRG (Barcelona Collaboratorium for Modelling and Predictive Biology), Barcelona, Spain.

author_details.name: Wagner A
author_details.affiliation: Department of Evolutionary Biology and Environmental Studies, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.; Swiss Institute of Bioinformatics, Lausanne, Switzerland.; The Sante Fe Institute, Sante Fe, New Mexico, United States of America.

abstract: The topography of fitness landscapes strongly influences the outcome of Darwinian evolution. This topography in turn is determined by the effects of genotypic changes on phenotypes, such as the structure and function of biomolecules like proteins and RNA. Thus, understanding the evolution of biomolecules requires an understanding of the relationship between genotype and phenotype. Here, we study how this relationship is influenced by the fundamental biochemical rules that determine which RNA bases can form base-pairs in RNA secondary structure. To this end, we computationally study the secondary structure genotype-phenotype maps of RNA molecules using all ten possible different such RNA base-pairing rules. We simulate adaptive evolution on fitness landscapes in which an RNA's fitness is defined by its secondary structure. We find that the base-pairing rules strongly affect how likely an evolving population is to find the global peak of a fitness landscape. The base-pairing rule of most biological RNA molecules (A-U, G-C, G-U) is among the top three most favorable rules for adaptive evolution, in which over 80% of evolving populations find a landscape's highest fitness peak. Simple characteristics of the genotype-phenotype map, such as the fraction of genotypes that constitute local peaks can help to predict how likely evolving populations are to find a landscape's global fitness peak. These characteristics can in turn be explained by two elementary properties of base-pairing rules that we call promiscuity and degeneracy.

title: Traction force microscopy using temporal information.

author_details.name: Hamaoka K
author_details.affiliation: Department of Science, Yokohama City University, Yokohama-City, Kanagawa, JAPAN.

abstract: Traction force microscopy is a simple, non-invasive method that can quantify cellular contact forces at the cell-substrate interface. It solves an inverse problem of determining the force field from measured substrate deformation. Because this problem is ill-posed with a large condition number, it is necessary to suppress the amplification of measurement noise during inversion. Previous studies have employed algorithms such as regularization or filtering that utilize spatial information to discriminate noise and true signals. Here, we propose an alternative approach that utilizes temporal information of the system. This method employs Kalman filter, a simple data assimilation algorithm in time series analysis, to recover the force field. Using numerically generated data, we show that the method is more accurate than standard algorithms including L2-regularization and is effective at filtering out temporal noise. Using experimental data on locomoting cells, we demonstrate that the method can reliably infer time-varying cellular traction forces. We also demonstrate two extensions of the proposed method: incorporation of additional knowledge and direct inference of low-dimensional force characteristics. These practical advantages will motivate the use of proposed framework for analyzing dynamic cell mechanics.

title: Vitamins E and C supplementation reduces hepatic lipid peroxidation and steatosis in neonatal Yucatan piglets receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition.

abstract: Parenteral nutrition (PN) is essential in neonatal care for many infants born prematurely or with impaired gastrointestinal function. However, prolonged PN use is associated with complications such as PN-associated liver disease and intestinal atrophy, potentially related to oxidative stress. Commercial PN lipid emulsions with fish oil are used to counteract PN-associated liver damage but may also contribute to oxidative stress due to their high content of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Using neonatal Yucatan miniature piglets as an established animal model for investigating PN-associated complications in neonates, this study investigated whether co-supplementation of vitamins E and C could reduce oxidative stress-related injury in the liver and small intestine during PN. The objective of this study was to determine whether supplementing a mixed-lipid emulsion (SMOFlipid®) with vitamins E and C would attenuate hepatic oxidative damage and enhance intestinal perfusion and morphology in neonatal piglets. Neonatal Yucatan piglets were surgically fitted with intravenous catheters and an indwelling blood flow probe around the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). Piglets received either standard PN (Control; n = 10) or PN supplemented with vitamins E (10 mg/kg/d) and C (100 mg/kg/d) (Vit E&C, n = 10) for ten days. Vitamin supplementation was associated with lower hepatic lipid accumulation and lipid peroxidation (P < 0.05 for both), compared with the control group. Plasma and liver vitamin E concentrations were markedly higher in the Vit E&C group (P < 0.001 and P < 0.01, respectively). No differences were determined between groups in liver or plasma triglyceride and cholesterol levels, SMA blood flow, intestinal villus height, crypt depth, or overall intestinal morphology. Hepatic and intestinal protein synthesis rates and in vivo bile acid clearance were also not significantly different between groups. Co-supplementation of PN with vitamins E and C was associated with lower hepatic oxidative stress and steatosis in neonatal piglets. Although no improvements were measured in intestinal structure or perfusion, these findings support the potential of antioxidant-enriched PN formulations to mitigate PN-associated liver complications.

abstract: This qualitative study aimed to explore the experiences of female patients following completion of orthodontic treatment with conventional fixed appliances and clear aligners. It used a clinical qualitative design with, semi-structured interviews featuring open-ended questions. Participants were recruited from private orthodontic practices, and the sample size was determined by data saturation. The final group included six patients treated with conventional fixed appliances and nine patients treated with clear aligners. Data were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using qualitative content analysis with peer validation of the categories. Seven categories emerged among patients treated with conventional fixed appliances: pain, discomfort, and hygiene difficulties; daily adaptations and restrictions; confidence in the professional; treatment duration; insecurity or embarrassment; desire to improve appearance; and satisfaction with treatment outcomes. For patients treated with clear aligners, seven categories were identified: practicality, comfort and hygiene; pain and discomfort related to use; treatment duration; willingness to recommend aligners; desire to improve appearance and appliance discretion; recommendation by the professional; and satisfaction. The findings show that, although patients with fixed appliances faced several challenges during treatment, aesthetic improvement was the main reason for seeking care, and overall satisfaction with the results was high. Patients who chose clear aligners aimed to avoid common limitations of fixed appliances and emphasized benefits related to comfort, convenience, oral hygiene, and discretion. These results highlight the importance of qualitative methods for understanding patient perspectives and can guide clinical communication and shared decision-making in adult orthodontic treatment.

abstract: Many RNA molecules function within confined environments, but the effect of confinement on RNA folding remains poorly understood. Proximity ligation experiments reveal altered long-range contacts in confined vs. unconfined states, yet they do not explain how spatial constraints give rise to these differences. Here, we develop a physical modeling approach that incorporates proximity ligation data into coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to reconstruct RNA 3D structures under confinement. We test our model on the [Formula: see text]11 kb genome of the Zika virus, comparing the folding in virions (confined) and in cells (unconfined). We observe that the probability of contact between two regions of the genome vs. linear distance follows different scaling laws in the confined and unconfined cases, in agreement with proximity ligation experiments. We find that genome circularization-an interaction that regulates replication in Zika-occurs more frequently under confinement in both experiments and simulations. Our model reveals that the formation of long double-stranded stems through stacking confers local nematic liquid crystalline order to the RNA, and predicts pseudoknot topologies consistent with those seen in crystallographic structures of shorter RNAs. These results provide insight into the mechanism through which confinement alters the ensemble of 3D structures accessible to a long RNA molecule.

abstract: Successful goal-directed behavior often requires the exertion of effortful cognitive control processes, but it remains unclear why engaging in cognitive control is experienced as effortful and induces fatigue. Here, we tested the hypothesis that sustained activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC)-a neural substrate of cognitive control-causally induces motivational fatigue via the accumulation of prefrontal glutamate metabolites. For this purpose, we combined brain stimulation with spectroscopy imaging to assess how increasing DLPFC excitability during an effortful mental task changes the motivation for mental effort and glutamate concentrations. We found that stimulating the DLPFC during mental effort exertion improved mental performance at the cost of increased posteffort motivational fatigue, suggesting a causal role of DLPFC activation for inducing fatigue. On the neural level, DLPFC activation during effortful cognition also increased prefrontal concentrations of glutamate, which statistically explained the fatigue-induced lower motivation for mental effort. A corresponding analysis of combined glutamate-glutamine (Glx) concentrations revealed converging effects. Together, these findings provide causal evidence that enhanced DLPFC activation contributes to fatigue via neurochemical changes, supporting neuro-metabolic accounts of fatigue and offering new insights into why demanding cognitive tasks are perceived as effortful.

abstract: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.

abstract: In temperate ecosystems, afforestation is rapidly expanding as a flagship climate mitigation strategy. Yet its impact on wildfires remains poorly understood, raising concerns that establishing planted forests over nonforest areas may intensify wildfire activity under increasingly fire-prone climatic conditions. Here, we combine land-use change data, fire activity records, climatic and anthropogenic covariates to quantify how afforestation alters fire occurrence and burned area across 67,248 patches distributed throughout global temperate biomes using satellite records starting in 2001. We found that, on average, afforestation increased fire occurrence by 26% and burned area by 23% in global temperate regions. However, these effects differed markedly among biomes. Wildfire responses ranged from a near-threefold increase in fire occurrence in Temperate Conifer Forests and a 38% increase in Mediterranean Woodlands biomes to an 18% reduction in the Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands biome. In Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests, afforestation reduced fire occurrence but increased burned area, indicating a shift toward less frequent but larger wildfires following the conversion to planted forest. These contrasting, biome-specific responses show that the consequences of afforestation on wildfire activity may depend strongly on ecological and regional context. The strong variability at biome-scale questions the premise that tree planting provides consistent climate mitigation benefits across all landscapes, and highlights the need to evaluate afforestation initiatives alongside regional disturbance regimes. Our findings indicate that wildfire risk should be explicitly accounted for when assessing the long-term effectiveness of afforestation as a climate mitigation strategy in a warming world.

abstract: European colonization introduced abrupt changes into the Americas. These included the introduction of infectious diseases, forced labor and displacement of Indigenous and African individuals, European settlement, and the imposition of caste regimes. However, the role of these forces in reshaping communities across different regions remains debated. This is especially true in the Virreinato del Río de la Plata (the territories of present-day Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, Paraguay, and Brazil), which is less studied than other regions such as the United States, the Caribbean, and Mexico. We investigated how these forces shaped the colonial societies of Mendoza in the Cuyo region (Central-Western Argentina) by sequencing ancient DNA of 28 individuals (17th to 19th centuries) excavated from churches associated with different social strata, recovering 22 mitochondrial genomes, and genome-wide data of 15 individuals. By performing paleogenomic analyses contextualized by burial site, we detected admixture among Indigenous, European, and African populations, with ancestry partially structured by church and burial location. Exceptions to this pattern indicate social mobility and flexible social classifications beyond genetic ancestry. The European-related ancestry aligns with Southern European migration, while African-related ancestry shows affinities to Western-Central Africa. The Indigenous-related ancestry shows highest affinity to precontact populations from Cuyo, supporting local genetic continuity across the colonial period. Additionally, uniparental markers reflect sex-biased dispersal and admixture. These findings reveal often-neglected African contributions to the city's formation and illustrate how caste, labor, and migration shaped colonial urban societies. Our work provides a scalable model for interrogating caste regimes, social mobility, and admixture in understudied regions of the Americas.

abstract: The relationship between evolution and allostery is inherently intertwined. While structural studies have elucidated allosteric mechanisms, the extent to which evolutionary sequence information encodes these dynamic networks remains underexplored. Here, we introduce Sequence-based GNM-TE, a framework that integrates coevolutionary information with Gaussian Network Model (GNM) based Transfer Entropy (TE) calculations. This approach translates evolutionary constraints, shaped by both structural and functional requirements, into functionally meaningful allosteric dynamic information. Across 29 cases, we identify binding sites as dynamic hubs of collective information transfer and reveal mode-dependent, directional information flows between these sites. These findings overall indicate that evolutionary constraints embed the architecture of allosteric regulation within protein sequences, preserving binding site communication within layered dynamic ensembles that enable robust functional control and adaptation.

abstract: In hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) caused by Hantaan virus (HTNV), virus-specific CD8 + T cells mediate both viral clearance and immunopathology. Here, we characterized a CD8 + regulatory T cell (Treg) subset restricted by HLA-E (and its murine ortholog Qa-1) in HFRS patients and in a murine HTNV infection model. CD8 + Tregs (CD122 + Eomes + CD49d lo KIR + ), a subset substantially enriched for HLA-E-restricted T cells, were significantly reduced in peripheral blood of HFRS patients and displayed a terminally differentiated profile with elevated expression of KLRG-1, NKG2A, CTLA-4, and Fas-L, correlating with disease severity. Two HTNV glycoprotein-derived nonapeptides that bound Qa-1 were identified. Following immunization with the identified HTNV peptides and subsequent HTNV challenge, wild-type (WT) mice showed attenuated renal immunopathology, whereas D227K knock-in mice (with disrupted Qa-1-CD8/TCR interaction) showed enhanced viral clearance in the spleen and kidney but exacerbated renal immunopathology. Mechanistically, Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs from WT mice suppressed effector CD8 + T cell proliferation in a peptide-specific, CD8/TCR-dependent manner via enhanced TGF-β secretion. Strikingly, D227K mutation dichotomously reshaped Treg phenotype: bulk polyclonal CD8 + Tregs displayed compensatory upregulation of inhibitory receptors (NKG2A, CTLA-4, PD-1) and TGF-β, whereas epitope-specific CD8 + Tregs showed impaired antigen-specific suppressive function and attenuated TGF-β production. Collectively, these findings indicate that HLA-E/Qa-1-restricted CD8 + Tregs can restrain immunopathology during HTNV infection, potentially at the cost of delayed viral elimination. Modulation of this axis may provide insights for therapeutic strategies in HFRS and related viral hemorrhagic fevers.

abstract: More than 65 years after the Brown v. Board of Education ruling that school segregation is unconstitutional, public schools across the United States are again experiencing rising segregation. In districts like San Francisco, efforts to implement district-wide choice policies have largely failed to reverse these trends. Since 2019, we have collaborated with the San Francisco Unified School District to design a student assignment policy meeting the district's goals of diversity, predictability, and proximity. We use optimization techniques to develop policies restricting choice to zones. We compare these to district-wide choice policies by estimating a choice model using historical application data and simulating assignment. Our results show multiple policies can reduce school segregation while preserving varying degrees of proximity, choice, and predictability. Zone-based policies with reserves reduce the concentration of racial minority students in high-poverty schools and maintain proximity, but reduce choice. District-wide choice with reserves and distance-based priority can further reduce segregation, but at the cost of predictability. Tradeoffs are necessary as no policy dominates another policy. In addition, we show that spatial segregation indices capture average patterns in these tradeoffs but miss important variation revealed by our simulation framework. Our work informed the design and approval of a zone-based policy in San Francisco in 2020, and supports ongoing policy implementation.

abstract: Climate change and variability push species to shift their distributions and phenology to track their climatic niche. Predicting population responses requires identifying the environmental cues that trigger reproduction, their fitness consequences, and the intrinsic factors that shape individual breeding decisions. In long-lived species with deferred breeding, extrinsic (environmental) and intrinsic (individual/maternal) factors may interact in shaping responses to environmental change, but direct empirical evidence remains scarce. We use 2065 breeding events collected over 22 y on a wide-ranging seabird, the Scopoli's Shearwater. We quantify the effects on population mean laying date of a large-scale climatic index (wNAO) associated with oceanographic conditions. We assess how individual breeding experience and mother-daughter resemblance contribute to among-female differences in reproductive timing, and evaluate the consequences for breeding success (BS) and adult survival. Average laying date was earlier under negative phases of wNAO, indicating a plastic response at the population level. Individual repeatability in the relative laying date (RLD) was high ( R = 0.50) irrespective of experience, indicating consistency among females. Using 142 mother-daughter cases, daughters' RLD resembled those of their mothers, a covariance that may reflect genetic inheritance, maternal effects, or shared environment. Early laying was associated with higher BS and survival, translating into an annual fitness advantage. Differences in survival and BS across individuals were more evident during the first observed breeding attempts. Together, these results support a scenario in which plasticity shifts the population mean breeding date in response to climatic variation, while persistent traits generate differential fitness among individuals.

abstract: Detection of endogenous biomolecules in vertebrate fossils remains controversial because labile compounds degrade quickly and are highly susceptible to contamination. Here, we present data on the preservation of heme-derived tetrapyrroles, and vascular canal-constrained ellipsoidal microstructures, inferred to be red blood cells, in limb bones of Aratasaurus museunacionali , a 115-million-year-old theropod dinosaur. High-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry identified parent and diagenetically altered heme B as the principal tetrapyrroles of bone extract, contrasting the chlorophyll and bacteriochlorophyll porphyrin signatures of the surrounding matrix supporting an endogenous origin. Separate spatially resolved analyses by Raman spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy confirmed the ellipsoid microstructure localization of i) porphyrin signals of heme and ii) key elements of heme (Fe, N, and C) and mineral stabilizing hausmannite (Mn 3 O 4 ), respectively. These results demonstrate blood-derived biomolecules in mineralized red blood cells of a dinosaur.
