abstract: T cells are essential for antitumor immunity, but their ability to eliminate tumors depends on interactions with type 1 conventional dendritic cells (cDC1s). cDC1s are known for cross-presenting tumor-derived antigens in lymph nodes to prime T cells, but their role within tumors remains less well understood. Here, we use a tumor array model to investigate how cDC1-T cell interactions influence immune responses and tumor fate. We show that the spatial distribution of both cDC1s and T cells determines whether a tumor can be rejected. We defined three immunotypes based on the spatial distribution of T cells and cDC1s: T cell-inflamed/dendritic cell-inflamed (TC-In/DC-In) tumors, where T cells and cDC1s coinfiltrate the tumor; T cell-inflamed/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-In/DC-Ex) tumors, where T cells infiltrate but cDC1s remain at the periphery; and T cell-excluded/dendritic cell-excluded (TC-Ex/DC-Ex) tumors, which lack both cDC1 and T cell infiltration. TC-In/DC-In tumors are most likely to undergo rejection, whereas TC-In/DC-Ex tumors persist despite T cell infiltration. Within TC-In/DC-In tumors, cDC1s interact directly with T cells, upregulate costimulatory molecules, and sustain effector T cell responses, while cDC1s in TC-In/DC-Ex tumors express higher migration-associated genes, suggesting they may exit the tumor. We further show that chemokine modulation, particularly through CXCL9, CCL5, and XCL1, can reshape immune infiltration patterns to promote intratumoral cDC1-T cell clustering and improve tumor rejection. These findings reveal an important role of cDC1 in sustaining effective antitumor immunity and highlight spatially organized cDC1-T cell clusters as critical hubs for local T cell activation.

abstract: System-level mapping of kinase inhibitors' polypharmacology can uncover opportunities for drug repurposing and identify starting points for medicinal chemistry campaigns aimed at novel targets. Here, we describe a large-scale profiling of 257 kinase inhibitors that revealed domains of promiscuity, a broad region of uninhibited targets and discrete pockets of selectivity. Focusing on a subcluster enriched for AGC group kinases and using the AKT inhibitor AT-7867 (an antiproliferative agent) as a starting point, we employed scaffold hopping and property-based optimization to discover NCGC-6782, a LATS1/2 inhibitor with robust proproliferative activity. In biochemical and cell-based assays, NCGC-6782 inhibited LATS1/2 activity, reduced YAP phosphorylation, and promoted rapid YAP nuclear translocation and transactivation of YAP-target genes. Kinome-wide profilings demonstrated good in vitro selectivity and exquisite chemoproteomic and kinetic selectivity. In vivo, NCGC-6782 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles following intraperitoneal (IP), intravenous (IV), or oral (PO) dosing, leading to rapid inhibition of YAP-phosphorylation in murine liver samples. Transcriptomics and proteomics following NCGC-6782 revealed upregulation of YAP-dependent genes (4 h) followed by activation of cell cycle programs (24 h). Consistently, NCGC-6782 accelerated proliferative regeneration in both cell-based and in vivo wound healing models of full-thickness excisional skin injury, significantly shortening wound-closure time without evidence of systemic toxicity. Altogether, we describe an optimized, potent, and selective LATS1/2 kinase inhibitor with desirable drug-like properties and broad potential for regenerative medicine applications following acute injury of nonproliferative, postmitotic tissues.

abstract: Although trust is fundamental to social interactions, how lifetime stressor exposure relates to the cognitive processes underlying trust remains poorly understood. Using the Stress and Adversity Inventory (STRAIN) to assess cumulative lifetime stressor exposure, combined with an adaptation of the repeated trust game and computational modeling (Hierarchical Gaussian Filtering), we investigated how stressors experienced over the life course relate to three core aspects of trust dynamics-initial trust formation, learning about others' intentions, and adaptation to changes in trustworthiness-in 168 adults. Greater lifetime stress was associated with stronger negativity biases, lower initial trust, and heightened uncertainty about others' intentions, increases that were general rather than specific to partner type. These more pessimistic priors were not accompanied by poorer reading of partners: Higher lifetime stress was associated with greater differentiation between prosocial and selfish trustees, driven by reduced investment in the selfish trustee alone. Computational analyses further indicated greater belief volatility, consistent with faster model-implied updating of perceived trustworthiness. These findings provide novel evidence that lifetime stress is associated with a profile consistent with recalibration, rather than a degradation, of the cognitive mechanisms underlying trust, with potential consequences for relationship formation and social functioning. They also provide a computationally grounded framework for understanding associations between adversity and social cognition and generate testable predictions for future experimental work.

abstract: Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer ( S )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structures of the full-length Vibrio harveyi CqsS dimer in the apo- and ATPγS-bound states. Our structures reveal the molecular basis for the initiation of the phosphorylation cascade, which we support through biochemical and genetic analyses. Autophosphorylation of CqsS occurs in cis at the conserved histidine residue (H1), whereas phospho-transfer to the conserved aspartate residue (D1) in the C-terminal receiver domain occurs in trans . By coexpressing CqsS and CqsA to capture CqsS bound to CAI-1, we unexpectedly find a tight interaction between the CqsS intracellular domain and CqsA. In the complex, the CqsS H1 residues are positioned away from the catalytic cavity, and CqsS kinase activity is inhibited. Cryo-EM analysis, focused on the transmembrane domain of CqsS in this complex, reveals the presence of two CAI-1 molecules. CAI-1 binding induces an obvious movement of transmembrane helix 6, disrupting its extension into the cytosol, providing a structural basis for how CAI-1 binding in the periplasm is coupled to signal transduction into the cytoplasm. Together, our findings advance the understanding of CqsS-CAI-1-mediated quorum-sensing signal transduction, an activity that underpins the coordination of group behaviors in vibrios.

abstract: Most microscopic descriptions of structural dynamics assume the Born-Oppenheimer separation, where electrons adjust adiabatically to ionic motion. When this separation breaks down, electronic and lattice degrees of freedom can evolve on different timescales, giving rise to new physical phenomena beyond the adiabatic limit. Here, we use time-resolved, phase-sensitive second-harmonic generation and pump-probe reflectivity to reshape the ferroelectric free-energy landscape of SnTe while separately tracking polar order and coherent lattice motion. When photoexcitation transiently suppresses the double-well barrier, polarization dynamics become strongly nonlinear, while the coherent phonon dynamics remain harmonic. This decoupling cannot be described by a single adiabatic coordinate for the electronic polarization and ionic positions. We provide a unifying physical description for the nonadiabatic dynamics of the ferroelectric mode and the mixed displacive/order-disorder nature of SnTe based on a separation of scales for the renormalization of the ferroelectric stiffness.

abstract: How the life of prehistoric people was influenced by climate change and extreme events often remains elusive. Finding appropriate spatiotemporal scales is the major challenge for studies with socioenvironmental questions. This challenge can be overcome by sourcing climatic information from archaeological sites, alongside traces of human agency. For instance, extreme cold-events have been proposed as causing a standstill in early farming expansion across the Mediterranean 8600-8000 years ago. However, there is no immediate (local/short-term) evidence of such events and how they might have influenced people's lives, nor have previous records been sufficiently resolved to test this robustly. Here we statistically assess the influence of on-site and short-term extremes on human decision-making hypothesized by long-term climate records. Using the largest dataset yet of high-resolution temperature archives in mollusks, we test whether early farmers would have been exposed to extreme cold-events, compromising their subsistence by reducing harvest yields. This immediate agricultural risk is argued to have prevented the spread of new settlements and thus delayed the vigorous expansion that followed, one of prehistory's fastest known dispersals. Direct comparison of paleotemperature and subsistence data from the same archaeological contexts shows no winter cooling of the magnitude proposed for this period, and no strong relationship between climate and subsistence. Our study reveals how a major scale mismatch in climate-society research can be resolved at the site level, integrating climatic variability on the subannual timescale crucial to farming, and provides a direct, local empirical test of a long-assumed climate impact.

abstract: Opiates slow colonic transit and cause constipation, effects traditionally attributed to suppression of excitatory cholinergic neurons through μ (MOR), δ (DOR), or κ (KOR) opioid receptors on myenteric neurons. However, the cellular mechanisms mediating opioid-induced constipation remain incompletely defined. We found that spontaneous enteric nitrergic motor inputs to mouse colon were reduced by opioid receptor agonists, leading to increased phasic contractions of colonic muscles, an effect abolished by pretreatment with tetrodotoxin, L-NNA, or apamin (in distal colon). Increased contractions in response to opioids are not easily explained by suppression of excitatory neural inputs, and spontaneous cholinergic motor inputs to colon were not suppressed by the MOR agonist Endomorphin-1 (EM-1). Consistent with these effects, MOR were expressed by many nitrergic neurons, and EM-1 reduced the asynchronous activity of nitrergic myenteric neurons during the period of tonic inhibition and the synchronized activity occurring normally just before neurogenic contractions. In addition to increasing phasic contractions, EM-1 enhanced Ca 2+ transients in interstitial cells of Cajal, depolarized membrane potentials of circular muscle cells, effects equivalent to the effects of tetrodotoxin. These are effects consistent with suppression of tonic inhibition. We also found that anterogradely propagating neurogenic contractions in intact colon were suppressed by receptor-specific MOR, DOR, and KOR agonists. Together, these observations demonstrate that opioid agonists suppress inhibitory rather than excitatory motor inputs to colonic muscles. Suppression of inhibitory motor inputs precludes the precisely timed cessation of enteric inhibition that causes poststimulus depolarization and peristaltic contractions.

abstract: Pericytes are phenotypically plastic and capable of switching between contractile and proliferative phenotypes, similar to vascular smooth muscle cells. The intimate interaction of contractile pericytes with endothelial cells (ECs) is essential to the maturation, quiescence, and stability of the capillary and microvascular endothelium. However, the mechanistic link between pericyte contraction and vascular stability is unknown. It is known that TGFβ has dual pro- and antiangiogenic effects depending on the downstream Smad signaling. Here, we show that R-Ras-mediated contractility in pericytes activates TGFβ by integrin-dependent, actomyosin-generated cell traction force. This TGFβ activation, in turn, promotes the quiescence of ECs via the ALK5-Smad2/3 axis of the TGFβ pathway in ECs, but not the Smad1/5 axis of the TGFβ pathway. Furthermore, pericyte-targeted deletion of Rras in mice resulted in impaired pericyte contractility and a significant reduction of Smad2/3 phosphorylation in ECs, accompanied by increased tumor angiogenesis and vessel deformation in the skeletal muscle. These observations suggest that pericytes use the cell force to maintain the quiescence of the endothelium by elevating the local bioavailability of active TGFβ. Our findings provide a mechanism by which pericytes stabilize blood vessels.

abstract: Polyethylene (PE)-like polyesters have long been investigated as biodegradable alternatives to conventional polyolefins but degrade poorly despite possessing hydrolyzable esters due to high crystallinity and hydrophobicity. Bees of the genus Colletes line their nests with a PE-like polyester that shows no environmental accumulation despite decades of nesting in dense aggregations, suggesting rapid biodegradability. This work provides a comprehensive characterization of Colletes inaequalis polyester and demonstrates its rapid degradation under ambient environmental conditions. Colletes polyester is completely insoluble in trichlorobenzene or toluene at elevated temperatures, indicating cross-linking despite originating from macrocyclic lactones that lack obvious cross-linkable functionality. Small molecules extracted from the network match the Dufour's gland secretion but lack macrolactone, indicating complete monomer conversion. Although its repeat unit resembles amorphous, network-like plant cutin, Colletes polyester is highly crystalline ( X c = 60%), with PE-like orthorhombic packing and T m = 75 °C, indicating a much lower cross-link density. Composition analysis of nest linings collected 0 to 11 mo after construction reveals significant degradation, with polyester content falling from 73 to 40 wt% within 4 mo in ambient soil. Esterase activity against the model substrate p-nitrophenylbutyrate is observed in both newly constructed and 4-mo aged linings, which may accelerate environmental degradation. Crystallites also lack higher-order spherulitic or lamellar structure, possibly due to cross-linking, which may promote degradation by leaving more esters exposed to cleavage. This PE-like polyester is shown to degrade rapidly in the environment, offering a template for next-generation biodegradable PE-like polymers.

abstract: The frequency and intensity of heat waves are increasing, but how these trends translate to changes in the ambient heat to which children are potentially exposed (hereafter, exposures) is not well established. One complicating factor is that it is not only extreme temperatures that change over time, but also the geospatial distribution of children. Another limitation in our understanding is that existing studies often summarize exposure as person-time accumulated above a temperature cutoff, a quantity that confounds the choice of cutoff, the duration of individual exposure, and the share of the population affected. Our study addresses these gaps by developing a double-dual-distributional framework that jointly considers two types of geospatial and temporal distributions (ambient temperatures and child populations) and two types of heat exposure thresholds, namely intensity (heat levels) and duration (hourly exceedance). To illustrate, we assessed potential exposures-the ambient heat conditions experienced-among 250 million children in China, comparing the 1989-1991 and 2019-2021 periods. We found that children's average annual exposure to moderate or stronger heat increased by 385 h, and the share exposed to strong heat for at least 12% of hours rose from 8.1% (24.9 million) to 23.7% (59.1 million). Both rising temperatures and shifts in child population distributions contribute materially to increased heat exposures in China, a finding that suggests the need for forecasts of children's potential heat exposures to consider shifting child population distributions.

abstract: Development of effective immune responses against any pathogen requires efficient activation of the innate immune system followed by induction of an appropriate adaptive immune response using specific signaling pathways tailored to each infection. The sole innate immune receptor implicated in the induction of adaptive immunity to retroviral infection is Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7). We have found that germinal center responses, neutralizing antibody production, and clearance of murine leukemia virus (MLV) infection in BALB.J and C57BL/6N (B6N) mice occurs in the absence of TLR7 signaling. This suggests that a previously unknown alternative sensing pathway exists for the activation of protective immune responses upon retroviral infection. Genetic crosses indicate that the ability to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling is determined by the same recessive mechanism in both B6N and BALB.J mice, suggesting that TLR7-independent responses do not result from a gain-of-function of an alternative pattern recognition receptor. Additionally, we observed that TLR7-deficient BALB.J mice produce neutralizing antibodies against mouse mammary tumor virus (MMTV) infection, indicating that this alternative sensing pathway is active against retroviruses of multiple genera. Finally, we determined that the alternative sensing pathway is also independent of both MyD88 and STING signaling. The ability of mice of two genetic backgrounds to control retroviral infection in the absence of TLR7 signaling provides a valuable tool for the identification of an additional mechanism of retrovirus control. The dissection of this pathway has the potential to alter our understanding of the requirements for the stimulation of antigen-specific neutralizing immunity.

abstract: Robust development requires maintaining correct proportions as overall size varies. What controls and limits this scaling remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of mechanical and biochemical embryonic factors. Combining confinement of dissociated embryonic presomitic mesoderm cells with imaging and chemical perturbations, we identified cell aggregation as the initial event in de novo posterior pole formation. Using a continuum model based solely on cell-cell attraction, we quantitatively map how the time available for aggregation-driven patterning limits the maximum scalable system size. Small systems allow rapid, robust pattern scaling, whereas coarsening dynamics substantially delay scaled patterns in large systems. Our experiments quantitatively confirm these predicted scaling regimes. Together, our results reveal a developmental time-size tradeoff governing the scaling of aggregation-driven patterns.

abstract: Rapidly rising temperatures threaten populations of ectothermic animals worldwide, with the greatest impacts predicted in the tropics-hotspots for biodiversity. Ectotherms can respond to warming through two primary compensatory responses: behavioral thermoregulation, which buffers exposure to extreme temperatures; and heat tolerance increases via plasticity, adaptation, or both. The relative contribution of these responses is predicted to depend on ecological context, but whether these principles can anticipate organismal responses to contemporary warming remains largely untested. Here, using a decadal resurvey of anole lizards from Hispaniola, Jamaica, and Puerto Rico, we show that simple principles of thermal ecology can reliably anticipate organismal responses to rising temperatures. Species occupying thermally heterogeneous open/edge habitats, such as dry forests, behaviorally thermoregulate and have shown little to no increase in heat tolerance over the past decade. By contrast, species from thermally homogeneous closed-canopy environments are poor thermoregulators and have increased their heat tolerance by 2 °C, on average, over the same period. Seasonal comparisons, acclimation experiments, and laboratory-rearing experiments indicate that contemporary increases in heat tolerance likely reflect contributions from rapid evolutionary change and physiological plasticity. Thermal ecology, not phylogenetic or spatial proximity, is the key factor driving responses to rising temperatures. Our results consistently link organismal responses to habitat complexity and thermoregulatory behavior; we suggest that these factors are key to predicting how ectotherms respond to climate warming.

abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) is an established treatment for depression, yet the fundamental question of how cortical stimulation influences single neurons in deep brain circuits critical for mood regulation remains unanswered. Using a rare opportunity to record from intracranial microelectrodes while TMS was delivered in four neurosurgical patients, we evaluated the responses of 185 single neurons. Artifact cleaning enabled single-neuron spikes to be resolved as early as 8 ms after stimulation. We found that single-pulse TMS to the left dlPFC elicited time-locked firing responses in 46% of neurons (26% facilitated only, 19% suppressed only, 1% both). These responses occurred within deep bilateral cortical and subcortical structures, including the putamen and thalamus. Single-pulse TMS tended to facilitate spiking in striato-thalamic putative inhibitory neurons from ~8 ms, peaking at ~80 to 100 ms, and decaying until ~600 ms. In contrast, putative excitatory neurons and limbic areas were suppressed with a slower time course lasting to ~1,000 ms. TMS-evoked potentials recorded from intracranial depth macroelectrodes to quantify network activity revealed that the modulation of responsive neurons was positively correlated with cortico-striato-thalamic network activity and anticorrelated with limbic network activity in one participant with sufficient network and unit sampling. These results suggest that dlPFC TMS recruits a high percentage of neurons spanning cortical and subcortical brain regions bilaterally. The recruitment pattern selectively involves increasing the firing rate of inhibitory neurons in executive control networks while suppressing limbic excitatory drive, providing a candidate cellular mechanism for how cortical stimulation modulates distributed brain networks.

abstract: Globally, cities account for 78% of energy consumption and 70~75% of greenhouse gas emissions. Using spatially explicit data on urban vegetation, water bodies, and buildings, combined with extensive daily observations of air temperature and electricity consumption for the subtropical megacity of Shenzhen, China, this study shows that urban nature contributes to urban cooling, reducing energy consumption and associated greenhouse gas emissions. We found that green and blue spaces in the city's built-up area had a pronounced influence on air temperature, ranging from a cooling effect of 1.27 °C to a warming effect of 0.29 °C, with the cooling effect being dominant over the course of a year. The cooling effect was greatest at moderate temperatures (~20 °C) and was lower on hotter days. We identified a temperature threshold of 16 to 18 °C above which urban nature produces measurable reductions in cooling energy demand. We found that residential electricity consumption was more temperature-sensitive than nonresidential electricity consumption. For the study year of 2021, the net electricity savings from urban nature was 1.5 billion kWh. This reduction in energy consumption translated to almost one million tons of avoided CO 2 emissions, which was 4.65-times the sequestration capacity of the city's terrestrial vegetation and equivalent to the annual emissions of over 223 thousand people using global average annual per capita carbon emissions.

title: A Scientific Claim Stability Framework for Evaluating MRI Morphometry Pipelines
abstract: MRI morphometry pipelines are often evaluated by measurement agreement or downstream accuracy, yet their scientific value depends on the conclusions they support. Two pipelines can produce similar feature-level results yet support different conclusions about aging, cognitive decline, or neurodegeneration. We introduce Scientific Claim Stability (SCS), a claim-centric evaluation framework that converts region-of-interest (ROI) morphometry tables into auditable claim cards and evaluates their support under changes in dataset, processing pipeline, atlas, feature family, and target. Across 10,370 MRI scans from three datasets and five cohorts, SCS generates 2,783 claim cards and evaluates 89 claim-family pairs. The evaluation distinguishes stable, transferable, and fragile claims. FreeSurfer 8-FastSurfer comparisons show high evidence concordance and low anatomical-support overlap under the primary covariate specification. Acquisition-adjusted analyses show that the magnitude of support disagreement depends on the model specification. Structured review by specialists in geriatrics, neuroscience, and radiology, alongside auxiliary ChatGPT and Gemini reviewers, assesses claim plausibility, clarity, faithfulness, usefulness, and caution. SCS provides a reproducible way to audit the evidential stability of morphometry claims without assuming a universal gold standard.

title: AVID: A 5T fMRI Dataset for Benchmarking Auditory-induced Visual Mental Imagery Decoding
abstract: Visual mental imagery (VMI) decoding uses brain activity to reconstruct internally generated visual scenes, providing a potential pathway for externalizing internal experiences and developing neuroprosthetic communication interfaces. However, progress is limited by the lack of dedicated, training-scale VMI datasets. Current VMI paradigms often rely on visual prompts or short-term memory images, introducing visual and mnemonic confounds that make it difficult to disentangle neural activity associated with endogenous image construction from signals driven by prior or concurrent visual input. Furthermore, existing VMI datasets offer limited descriptive control over individual visual attributes, making it difficult to systematically assess fine grained visual details. To address these gaps, we introduce AVID, the first dedicated training-scale 5.0 Tesla functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) resource for auditory-induced VMI decoding. AVID comprises approximately 67 hours of dense recordings from nine participants. The dataset is structured into two complementary splits: a scene-level complex split using naturalistic Mandarin descriptions and a controlled simple split with explicitly specified visual attributes. We further formalize a standardized evaluation protocol that decouples source-image consistency from semantic alignment, allowing for a more nuanced assessment of imagery reconstruction. Baseline qualitative and quantitative results show that current reconstruction pipelines remain limited on AVID, although the most successful reconstructions preserve recognizable scene level semantics from spoken descriptions. By combining dedicated training-scale neural recordings and standardized evaluation resources, AVID provides both a data foundation for imagery-specific model development and a benchmark for evaluating VMI decoding with substantially reduced sensory contamination.

title: Attribution-based diagnostics for single-cell foundation models
abstract: Single-cell RNA foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for in-silico biological discovery, yet predictive performance alone does not reveal whether their decisions rely on biologically meaningful signals or model-specific shortcuts. We systematically investigate post-hoc attribution of downstream predictions across two tasks: cell-type annotation using pretrained Cell2Sentence and scGPT models, and perturbation prediction using scGPT+STATE in a controlled setting. For cell annotation, we use attribution to assess whether predictions rely on established marker genes and how their relevance varies with model architecture, expression rank, and the surrounding cellular context. For perturbation prediction, we compare attribution patterns with known regulatory ground-truth in a synthetic setting to assess what they reveal about the model's learned computations. Across these tasks, attribution reveals biological feature use, contextual interactions, contributions from different input pathways, learning progression, associations with prediction quality, and potential pitfalls that are not fully captured by standard performance metrics. Experiments with complete and limited regulatory knowledge further demonstrate that conclusions drawn from attribution depend strongly on the choice of biological reference, baseline, and null model. Together, these findings highlight the value of attribution as a flexible post-hoc diagnostic for understanding model behavior, identifying potential issues, and informing the development of scFMs.

title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
abstract: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.

title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure. Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. Linear readouts fitted to frozen representations can match or exceed models' native outputs, and functional post-training substantially improves the models' capabilities. Linear readouts transfer well across experimental assays and genes, suggesting that models capture functional patterns beyond the data used to fit individual predictors. At the same time, strong prediction of average effects can conceal weaker prediction of context-specific effects, and accurate prediction of combined mutation effects does not imply accurate prediction of their interactions. In design tasks, model predictions can reduce the number of candidates needed to find a desired response, but still leave substantial room for better design choices, particularly for context-specific and multi-cell objectives. Our benchmark reveals that genomic models now display signs of general utility but have yet to saturate on performance in even simple tasks.

title: Coupling cellular trajectories and RNA kinetics on continuous expression manifolds with ManifoldVelo
abstract: Jointly recovering pseudotime and RNA velocity from static single-cell transcriptomes requires reconciling global trajectory structure with local expression changes, particularly in complex cycles and branching differentiation. Here we introduce ManifoldVelo, a topology-conditioned framework that jointly learns cellular coordinates, continuous RNA trajectories and regulatory kinetics. Derivatives of unspliced and spliced RNA trajectories are matched to transcription-splicing-degradation dynamics, including between observed cells, allowing expression reconstruction, cellular ordering and kinetic estimation to inform one another. ManifoldVelo recovers pseudotime across all evaluated single-cell trajectory types, including cyclic, multibranch and smooth non-branching trajectories. ManifoldVelo achieves the best pseudotime recovery among compared methods in multipeak cyclic simulations and the highest directional agreement for spliced RNA velocity in both multipeak cyclic and branching simulations. Real-data analyses support phase prediction across experimental plates and differentiation trajectories consistent with pancreatic developmental stages and marker expression. Its central advantage is the joint recovery of temporal position and local dynamics across distinct trajectory structures within a reusable dynamic reference. New cells are assigned pseudotime and velocity predictions from spliced RNA alone, without refitting the reference model. ManifoldVelo provides a foundation for dynamic cell atlases that transfer learned temporal and kinetic information to new samples.
