title: State-dependent emergence of coupling between oscillatory and aperiodic neural activity
abstract: Neural oscillations and aperiodic activity are two quintessential mesoscopic-level features arising from shared circuits, yet what governs their relationship remains unclear. Here we show that coupling between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent is sporadic and state-dependent. Bias-reduced analyses of 3,245 intracranial contacts from 61 awake subjects showed significant coupling in only <13% of contacts per band. A connectome-constrained dynamical model predicted that neither changes of input to local circuit nor removal of long-range connections modulated the coupling; whereas stronger local inhibitory feedback drove covariation between oscillatory frequency and aperiodic exponent. The model predictions were supported by three independent experiments: transcranial stimulation shifted each component independently and focal ablation of remote cortical tissues did not change coupling; whereas coupling emerged during seizures that altered local excitatory-inhibitory balance. These results suggest that the relation between periodic and aperiodic neural activity is neither intrinsically independent nor coupled, but determined by local circuit states.

title: Strategy-dependent causal relationships between large-scale cortical activity and perceptual decisions
abstract: Animals can adopt different internally generated strategies to solve decision-making tasks, but whether cortical regions distinctly contribute to decisions under different strategies remains unknown. To address this problem, we analyzed three datasets comprising either cortical widefield imaging, or optogenetic inactivation of dozens of cortical locations in 54 mice, all performing the same sensory-evidence-accumulation task. Using Generalized Linear Model-Hidden Markov Models (GLM-HMMs), we found that the mice adopted one of three underlying strategies: an engaged, stimulus-driven state, and two disengaged states characterized by large side biases. The specific effects of inactivation of cortical regions depended on behavioral strategy: during engaged states, inactivation tended to increase side bias, while the opposite was true in biased states. For engaged states, these effects were most prominent when frontal regions were inactivated. Moreover, neural decoding analyses from cortex-wide activity revealed that frontal regions preferentially encode the animals' choices during engaged states relative to biased states. Our results suggest that distinct patterns of large-scale cortical dynamics underlie decisions under different task strategies and identify the frontal cortex as an important substrate of engaged-strategy control.

title: Striatal and frontal signatures of social context and cost-benefit decision making in developmental stuttering
abstract: Developmental stuttering is usually framed as a sensorimotor disorder, yet it manifests in communicative situations that engage motivational, self-referential, and regulatory processes. In this case-control study, we combined a socio-economic decision task outside the scanner with a socially modulated speech task during functional MRI to test how listener presence and self-referential speech shape neural activity in 34 adults who stutter and 32 controls. Both groups valued talking with another person about themselves more than talking with another person about someone else or talking to themselves. On the neural level, listener-directed (vs. private) speech and self-disclosure (vs. guessing the preferences of a famous other) elicited stronger responses in the ventral striatum and medial prefrontal cortex, with no significant group differences in the central listener-directed versus private contrast. Within the stuttering group, individual differences revealed a systematic reweighting of socially modulated activation as a function of symptom burden: higher anticipation of stuttering and greater self-reported impact of stuttering on everyday life were associated with stronger engagement of motivational circuitry, greater recruitment of frontal evaluative-control regions, and reduced contextual differentiation within speech-language cortex. Stuttering anticipation and lived experience gradually shift the balance between control, language, and motivational salience-processing systems, contributing to the disorder's marked heterogeneity and context sensitivity. These findings indicate system-level signatures of the interaction between social context and symptom severity in developmental stuttering, extending accounts based on sensorimotor deficits.

title: Structure-Based Discovery of GTP-Enhanced Rab10 Modulators and Their Effects on Alzheimer Disease-Relevant Cellular Phenotypes
abstract: Rab10-mediated membrane trafficking has been implicated in Alzheimer disease (AD), but pharmacological tools for investigating its function remain limited. Here, we screened more than 80 million compounds using structure-based virtual screening and prioritized five candidate Rab10 modulators (R1-R5). These compounds exhibited favorable docking scores, stable modeled protein-ligand complexes in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and predicted acceptable ADME/toxicity profiles. Comparative docking against Rab5, Rab8, and Rab11 predicted preferential interactions with GTP-associated Rab10. R1 and R2 yielded the most favorable Rab10 scores, whereas R3 showed the largest differences between GTP-associated, GDP-containing, and nucleotide-free Rab10 models. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) revealed micromolar apparent affinities of R1-R4 without added GTP and nanomolar apparent affinities under GTP-containing conditions, generally favoring GTP-bound Rab10 over Rab5. In a cell-based GTP quantification assay, R1, R2, R3, and R5 reduced GTP-bound Rab10, whereas R4 increased it. R3 produced dose- and time-dependent reductions in GTP-bound Rab10 and was selected for functional studies. R3 altered endosomal organization and reduced EEA1 and LAMP1 expressions. In amyloid precursor protein (APP)/presenilin-1-expressing CHO cells, R3 redistributed intracellular APP, reduced APP carboxyl-terminal fragments (APP-CTFs), and decreased enlarged endosome-like structures. In neuronal differentiated PC12 cells, R1-R3 attenuated NGF withdrawal-induced cytoskeletal disruption and cell death, accompanied by reduced APP-CTF accumulation and tau phosphorylation. These studies highlight novel Rab10 modulators and support their further validation as candidate pharmacological probes for investigating Rab10-associated trafficking and AD-relevant cellular phenotypes.

title: Summed contrasts can conceal reversed regional preferences: directional and dose criteria for screening transcranial direct current stimulation montage pairs
abstract: Background: The regional-matching design evaluated here requires two transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) montages, each stronger in its own target region, with adequate exposure. Summed contrasts can be positive when only one preference holds. Objective: To test whether a summed double-dissociation index (DDI), overlap and cohort-median dose rules identify such pairs, for a focused-attention versus open-monitoring experiment. Methods: Twenty-four montage pairs were simulated in 20 anatomical head models (SimNIBS 4.6, 2 mA). A four-rule screen (DDI, overlap, cohort-median dose) was recorded before cohort results; a post hoc conjunction required both regional contrasts positive in >=80% of heads. Two leading pairs were compared on per-head dose, a second solver and 60 conductivity stress-test draws. Results: Eighteen pairs passed the screen, but 13 failed the conjunction; one with positive median DDI (0.782) reversed the salience-region preference in all 20 heads. The nominated pair (F3-centered 4x1 ring; F8-Fp2 sponges; median DDI 1.561; both preferences in 20/20 heads) brought both anatomical targets to the 0.20 V/m operational floor in 11/20 heads; a conventional sponge pair (DDI 0.627) did so in 20/20, though both passed the cohort-median dose rule. The nominated pair's separation held across a second solver and all 60 stress-test draws, but both network targets reached the floor in 19/60. Conclusions: Summed indices and cohort-median dose rules can pass pairs that fail reciprocal-exposure criteria. Such screens should pre-specify the directional conjunction and report per-head joint dose coverage. These are modeled exposures, not physiological or behavioral effects.

title: Surprisal contributes little beyond contextual embeddings in high-gamma ECoG encoding
abstract: Surprisal and contextual embeddings are both derived from large language models and are widely used to predict neural responses during language comprehension, but it is unclear whether surprisal adds information beyond embeddings. We test this directly: does word surprisal improve out-of-sample prediction of high-gamma ECoG responses after GPT-2 XL contextual embeddings are included? Using public ECoG recordings from natural speech, we fit word-aligned ridge encoding models with baseline stimulus features, GPT-2 XL embeddings, and GPT-2 XL surprisal. Adding one surprisal predictor left held-out correlation essentially unchanged at the primary response window, and the increment stayed within an equivalence margin across alternative lags, residualized surprisal, and frequency-band targets; it did not uniformly meet the same criterion under banded ridge regularization or within labeled temporal subsets. This small increment suggests that surprisal does not act as an independent predictor. It is better understood as a compressed readout of the same broader predictive state that the embeddings already capture.

title: Systematic Spike Sorting Errors Revealed by Juxtacellular Ground Truth in the Awake Brain
abstract: Existing ground-truth data for spike sorting come almost entirely from anesthetized or in vitro preparations. Yet phenomena expected to challenge spike sorting most (spike overlap and bursting) depend on brain state and differ in the awake brain. Therefore, error estimates from existing benchmarks may not transfer to awake recordings, and the types of errors in the awake brain remain largely uncharacterized. To address this, we generated a ground-truth dataset (16 neurons) using paired juxtacellular-extracellular electrophysiology in awake mice, and found spike sorting performance, particularly recall, to be lower than conventional benchmarks might suggest. Generally, false negatives sharply increased with intrinsic physiological factors like bursting, whereas false positives were more strongly associated with extrinsic factors, such as putative spike overlaps. To quantify contributions to errors from intrinsic and extrinsic factors, for each observed juxtacellular waveform we predicted the corresponding extracellular waveform. In the best-performing sorter, we estimate approximately half of false positives were attributable to credulous attempts to resolve putative overlaps. Bursting and putative overlaps were each associated with a roughly doubled false negative rate when they occurred separately, and with a sevenfold increase when they occurred together. These co-occurrences accounted for approximately 40% of a typical neuron's false negatives, despite comprising only approximately a fifth of its spikes. Thus, the moments when spike sorters must rely on the assumption of waveform invariance the most to resolve overlaps are exactly the moments when bursting makes that assumption least valid. We also estimate that three-quarters of false negatives had been detected but assigned to other units. These spikes were not cleanly oversplit: post-hoc merging was not productive because the loss in precision was three times the gain in recall. Because bursting and spike overlaps often co-occur, sorting spikes by waveform similarity and repairing the result by post hoc merging is unlikely to adequately balance precision and recall in the situations of greatest scientific interest. That is, while bursting and spike overlaps may involve only a minority of spikes, the resulting sorting errors may disproportionately distort the interpretation of neuronal population dynamics. We thus conclude that uncertainty quantification in sorters' output is essential.

title: TRPV4 antagonist efficacy in a post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus pig model
abstract: Hydrocephalus occurs across the age spectrum but is particularly prevalent in young and old individuals. One form of this disease is post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus (PHH), which is a life-threatening sequela of intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH). There are no effective non-surgical interventions for the treatment of PHH or other forms of hydrocephalus. Progress has been limited by the lack of gyrencephalic animal models that exhibit high fidelity to human conditions. Here, we establish a pathophysiologically relevant novel swine model of IVH that recapitulates key features of severe PHH, including sustained ventriculomegaly, elevated intracranial pressure (ICP), neuroinflammation and white matter injury. Using this model, we test the therapeutic potential of pharmacologic inhibition of the transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) non-specific cationic channel. The orally bioavailable TRPV4 antagonist GSK2789917 penetrates the blood-brain barrier, and prevents progression to PHH when administered 2 days after IVH. Specifically, GSK2789917 prevents the development of ventriculomegaly, suppresses early ICP elevations and prevents or reverses inflammasome activation. These findings establish a clinically relevant large-animal model of PHH and identify TRPV4 antagonism as a promising treatment for hydrocephalus.

title: The anti-dyskinetic and the anti-parkinsonian effects of sub-anesthetic ketamine are also present in female preclinical models
abstract: Biological sex is an important determinant of neuropharmacological response, yet females remain underrepresented in preclinical studies of Parkinson's disease (PD) and L-DOPA-induced dyskinesia (LID). We previously demonstrated that sub-anesthetic ketamine reduces established LID, attenuates dyskinesia development, and produces anti-parkinsonian effects in male unilateral 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA) rat models. However, whether these therapeutic effects extend to females remained unknown. Here, we evaluated the anti-dyskinetic and anti-parkinsonian effects of sub-anesthetic ketamine in female Sprague-Dawley rats using the attenuation and established models of LID. In the attenuation paradigm, unilateral 6-OHDA-lesioned females received repeated L-DOPA administration with either ketamine (20 mg/kg, i.p.; 10-h dosing paradigm) or vehicle. Ketamine significantly attenuated the progressive development of dyskinesia, indicating that early intervention modified the trajectory of LID expression. In the established LID paradigm, ketamine produced robust significant acute reductions in abnormal involuntary movements (AIMs) after dyskinesia had fully developed, and these significant effects persisted for up to 49 days following treatment, demonstrating sustained suppression of dyskinesia severity. To determine whether ketamine altered therapeutic motor function, forelimb adjusting steps testing was performed in female unilateral 6-OHDA rats. Ketamine did not impair L-DOPA-mediated motor improvement suggesting compatibility with the gold standard medication. Ketamine was also by itself associated with significantly improved stepping performance during ketamine treatment conditions, indicating acute anti-parkinsonian motor benefit. Together, these findings demonstrate that the anti-dyskinetic and anti-parkinsonian effects of ketamine extend to female preclinical models and strengthen the translational rationale for repurposing sub-anesthetic ketamine as a potential therapeutic strategy for individuals with LID.

title: Topographic reference modelling of white matter hyperintensities across the adult lifespan
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are among the most common MRI findings in older adults. They are widely regarded as markers of brain aging and cerebral small-vessel disease, and associated with risk for cognitive decline, Alzheimers disease and related dementias (ADRD), and stroke. White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are typically interpreted by total lesion burden, but lesions with similar volumes can occupy different anatomical locations, potentially reflecting distinct pathological processes. Here we present voxelwise topographic reference modelling (vTRM), a framework for characterizing individual WMH masks against age- and sex-stratified frequency maps derived from cognitively unimpaired individuals. Using 42,469 FLAIR-derived lesion masks from twelve adult cohorts, we mapped population-level WMH spatial vulnerability, characterized age-related changes in its distribution across periventricular, lobar and arterial-territory compartments, and constructed paired percentile charts for lesion burden and spatial typicality. A quadrant-based classification defined by these two percentile dimensions revealed graded relationships with ADRD pathophysiology, neurodegeneration, and cognitive impairment, while identifying WMH patterns differentially associated with ageing-related, vascular and neurodegenerative processes among individuals with similar lesion volumes. These reference charts establish a benchmark for normative WMH ageing, enabling quantification of individual deviations from typical age-, sex- and burden-related patterns and identification of WMH phenotypes associated with vascular, neurodegenerative or mixed etiologies. The framework, together with a deployable 3D U-Net model trained on these data for automated WMH segmentation, is available through the Brain Lesion Analytics platform (https://brainlesionanalytics.org/).

title: Transcranial alternating current stimulation reverses adolescent alcohol-induced cellular and behavioral deficits.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcohol is commonly consumed by adolescents in a binge-like pattern that can produce persistent cognitive impairments. Previous work found that adolescent intermittent ethanol (AIE) exposure reduces parvalbumin expressing (PV+) interneurons and increases perineuronal net (PNN) expression in brain regions critical for cognition. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), a noninvasive neuromodulation technique, has shown promise for treating psychiatric disorders associated with cognitive dysfunction. Here, we examined whether AIE exposure alters PV+ interneurons and PNN expression in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and impairs cognition, and whether mPFC-targeted gamma tACS can reverse these effects. METHODS: Sprague Dawley rats (N=139, 50% female) underwent AIE or control exposure during adolescence and received Active or Sham mPFC-targeted gamma tACS treatment for three consecutive days in adulthood. Following stimulation, rats either underwent immunohistochemical assessment of PV+ and PNN expression or behavioral testing using the novel object recognition (NOR) task. RESULTS: AIE exposure reduced PV+ cell counts in the prelimbic cortex, an effect that was reversed by active tACS. In contrast, AIE exposure did not alter PNN measures. Interestingly, active tACS affected the prelimbic and infralimbic cortices more than the anterior cingulate cortex. AIE exposure also reduced recognition memory of a novel object, and this deficit was ameliorated by active tACS when assessed one week after stimulation. Additionally, active stimulation decreased anxiety-like behavior in the open-field test. CONCLUSIONS: Together, these results confirm that adolescent alcohol exposure produces lasting cellular and cognitive alterations and supports mPFC-targeted gamma tACS as a potential intervention for alcohol-induced dysfunction.
author_corresponding_institution: Bowles Center for Alcohol Studies, School of Medicine, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, NC, USA

title: Transplantation of human iPSC-derived retinal cells in the cone-dominant Northern tree shrew
abstract: Abstract: Purpose: To characterize the transplantation and survival of photoreceptors generated from human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived retinal organoids in the Northern tree shrew (Tupaia belangeri, TS). Methods: TS eyes were injected with retinal cells dissociated from GFP-expressing hiPSC-derived retinal organoids (12 animals; n=22 eyes). 15 eyes had prior damage induced by either experimental retinal detachment (n=11) or ATP-induced retinal damage (n=4), and seven eyes were undamaged. Retinal organoids were treated with Notch pathway inhibitor 2 days before transplant. TS retinal structure and cellular details were assessed post-transplantation for up to 8 weeks using scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (SLO), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and adaptive optics SLO (AOSLO). Histological analysis was done at the end of the experiment. Results: Cell transplants in eyes treated with a simple immunosuppression treatment failed to survive for more than 2 weeks (n=10 eyes). Robust cell survival was observed in the eyes treated with a complex immunosuppression cocktail for up to 8 weeks (n=12 eyes). The transplanted cells were confirmed to be subretinally located using OCT imaging and the cell fate was confirmed to be human photoreceptors by histology. Finally, AOSLO imaging captured structures resembling photoreceptor inner segments. Conclusions: Our results demonstrate survival of transplanted cells using a species-specific immunosuppression treatment. Future studies should aim to explore the long-term survival and function of the transplanted cells.

title: Turning an object into a scene: buildings activate scene-selective visual cortex independently of visual features
abstract: Human visual cortex contains regions that selectively respond to both scenes and large objects, particularly buildings. The cortical overlap between buildings and scenes has been attributed to shared visual features (e.g., cardinal orientations, rectilinearity). Alternative accounts propose that buildings may also activate scene representations indirectly, independently of specific visual features, for example because buildings evoke a sense of space. Here, we tested for such feature-independent activation by comparing EEG and fMRI responses in human participants (both sexes) to buildings and visually-matched boxes, and relating these responses to scene-selective responses. Buildings and boxes were matched using image-based metrics, deep neural networks, and a perceptual similarity task. Time-resolved EEG decoding showed that buildings and boxes evoked discriminable responses from 360ms post-stimulus onset, incompatible with feedforward visual feature processing. Importantly, the building-box classifier generalized to discriminate scenes from chairs, providing the first EEG evidence for a representational overlap between buildings and scenes. Temporal generalization analyses further showed that the late building-selective response corresponded to an earlier scene-selective response, with a temporal offset of ~130ms. Finally, ultra-fast fMRI (TR=140ms) revealed that the scene-selective parahippocampal place area (PPA) similarly showed a feature-independent building-selective response that was delayed and prolonged relative to the scene-selective response. These results clarify the nature of building selectivity in visual cortex by showing that this selectivity is feature-independent and delayed relative to scene selectivity. We propose that intrinsic associations between object categories (e.g., buildings and scenes, tools and hands) may account for part of the categorical organization of ventral temporal cortex.

title: Ultradeep optical coherence tomography
abstract: Deep optical imaging of intact brain tissue is limited by scattering and absorption, restricting our ability to study subcortical structures. Here, we introduce ultradeep optical coherence tomography (OCT), which combines hardware and computational approaches to enhance the signal from deep tissue regions. Ultradeep OCT utilizes a longer illumination center wavelength of 1575 nm, spectral-domain balanced detection and imaging in the conjugate configuration with the zero optical path difference positioned deep in the tissue. Autocorrelation artifacts are measured and subtracted, and multiple frames are coherently averaged to improve the signal-to-noise ratio further. These techniques, along with computational refocusing and bandwidth control, allowed us to extend structural imaging depth in biological tissues. Ultradeep OCT demonstrated physical imaging depths of 2.3 to 2.8 mm (mean 2.5 mm) in the ex vivo mouse brain and 2.5 to 3.0 mm (mean 2.8 mm) in chicken tissue. The resulting volumes in the ex vivo mouse brain samples depict the dorsal hippocampus and its two major subregions with sufficient contrast to allow segmentation and three-dimensional reconstructions. Features in the thalamus could also be discerned. These findings demonstrate the potential of ultradeep OCT as a label-free approach for visualizing deep-brain structures at a spatial scale complementary to magnetic resonance imaging and microscopy. This approach could enable optical imaging studies of hippocampal structural changes in mouse models of neurodegenerative disease.

title: Unpredictable chronic stress redistributes novelty-evoked exploratory space use and yields method-dependent identification of resilient-like archetypes in zebrafish
abstract: Unpredictable chronic stress (UCS) produces heterogeneous behavioural outcomes, but identifying resilient individuals remains challenging because post-stress behaviour is multidimensional and classification depends on the analytical framework. We characterised novelty-evoked exploration in 178 adult zebrafish (89 unstressed reference, 89 UCS-exposed) using four Novel Tank Test variables: distance travelled, line crossings, upper-zone entries and upper-zone time, from a historical LAPCOM dataset from four independent cohorts. Behaviour was robustly normalised to control distributions within cohorts. In the unstressed population, principal component analysis revealed a dominant exploratory gradient (PC1 = 74.9%; PC2 = 18.7%), whereas weighted k-nearest-neighbour Louvain analysis yielded a stable two-profile partition. However, null-model inference and resampling did not support discrete behavioural populations, indicating a predominantly continuous reference architecture. UCS significantly redistributed individuals within this architecture (PERMANOVA: F(1,173) = 8.10, R2= 0.0423, p = 0.0016), reducing occupancy of the higher-exploration reference profile from 55.1% to 24.7%, while multivariate dispersion, Mahalanobis distance and global correlation structure showed no detectable differences. De novo Louvain analysis identified lower- and higher-exploration configurations, but correspondence with the control reference was asymmetric: all 44 lower-exploration fish mapped to the lower reference profile, whereas only 22 of 45 higher-exploration fish mapped to the higher reference profile. Thus, higher exploration after UCS was insufficient to define a resilient-like response. Across five analytical frameworks, resilient assignments ranged from 9 to 45 individuals and susceptible assignments from 23 to 68, with partial individual-level convergence. These findings support reference-integrated behavioural stratification for identifying resilient- and susceptible-like candidates for physiological, cellular and molecular validation.

title: Visual-cortex-projecting neurons in mouse auditory cortex show distinct audiovisual responses independent of motor-related activity
abstract: Cells in mouse primary visual cortex (V1) not only respond to visual stimulation, but also to sound. Part of this auditory modulation likely originates from auditory cortex (AC). Yet, the circuit-level functionality of the AC-to-V1 projection remains poorly understood. Here we performed acute in vivo high-density recordings in mouse AC during auditory, visual, and audiovisual stimulation, identifying AC-to-V1 projecting neurons by optogenetic tagging. Compared to non-tagged neurons, AC-to-V1 neurons more often responded to auditory, visual, or audiovisual stimuli. Furthermore, most AC-to-V1 neurons responded to specific sound frequencies; a modest but significant fraction was selective for visual orientations. These results could not be explained by motor responses or single-neuron variations in firing rate, cortical recording depth, or waveform type. These findings show that AC-to-V1 neurons carry sensory-specific signals, as opposed to nonspecific modulations, and exhibit distinctive response profiles compared to non-tagged AC neurons.

title: Why probe registration is crucial for infant fNIRS and HD-DOT? An evaluation across 49 newborns
abstract: Source-detector probe registration, i.e., the mapping of optode positions on the scalp to their true anatomical locations in head/brain space, is crucial for brain imaging with fNIRS or HD-DOT. While individual, MRI-based registration is desirable, it is not always feasible, motivating the development of alternative registration approaches. This study uses the STORM-Net registration protocol and quantifies the variation of cap alignment in a cohort of 49 newborns to evaluate how this affects reconstructed images using HD-DOT. Relative to a centrally aligned template, the cohort showed a median probe-position error of 10.12 mm, while the least and most misaligned subjects exhibited mean errors of 4.41 mm and 20.60 mm, respectively. The results demonstrate that the level of cap misalignment typically observed in newborn imaging can affect the spatial accuracy of reconstructed functional images, particularly in cases with larger probe displacements. These findings provide a quantitative basis for adopting more conservative interpretations of group-level functional brain activity and functional connectivity results, and strongly support the routine use of registration methods in infant HD-DOT studies.

title: Wolffia globosa -derived nanovesicles as a natural source of bioactive metabolites with neuroprotective potential against methylglyoxal-induced oxidative stress
abstract: Plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) have attracted increasing attention for their potential biomedical applications, particularly in oxidative stress-related diseases and neuroprotection. Wolffia globosa, an emerging functional food and potential future food source, is rich in phytochemicals associated with health-promoting properties. Harnessing W. globosa-derived nanovesicles (WGNVs) represents a promising strategy for expanding the biomedical applications of this plant. In this study, WGNVs were isolated and characterized, and their neuroprotective potential was evaluated in vitro. The isolated WGNVs exhibited nanoscale dimensions and a lipid bilayer structure. Biochemical analyses revealed substantial total phenolic and flavonoid contents, alongside intrinsic antioxidant activities. Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified a diverse repertoire of metabolites, including major constituents subsequently validated using independent analytical approaches. These findings provided a foundation for investigating the neuroprotective effects of WGNVs in a methylglyoxal (MGX)-induced model of neuronal oxidative stress. High-resolution confocal microscopy demonstrated the cellular localization of WGNVs within neuronal cells, providing evidence of interactions between plant-derived nanovesicles and neuronal cells. WGNV treatment attenuated MGX-induced free radical accumulation and oxidative stress responses while preserving cellular morphology integrity. Collectively, this study provides foundational evidence of the physicochemical characteristics, metabolite composition, and in vitro neuroprotective potential of WGNVs. These findings highlight WGNVs as a promising naturally derived nanocarrier platform for investigating plant-animal interkingdom interactions and exploring potential therapeutic applications across a broad range of biomedical fields.

abstract: A substantial fraction of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated proteins remains poorly characterized, in part because of the limited availability of validated research antibodies. We established knockout (KO)-based antibody characterization workflows and demonstrated that widely used antibodies against the major ALS-associated protein C9orf72 lacked specificity (Laflamme et al., 2019). We subsequently scaled this framework to systematically benchmark research antibodies, revealing that up to 61% fail to perform as recommended by manufacturers (Ayoubi et al., 2023b). Here, we extend this approach by establishing the ALS-Reproducible Antibody Platform (ALS-RAP), a comprehensive effort to generate a publicly available dataset of KO-validated antibodies targeting proteins encoded by ALS risk genes. In total, we characterized 303 antibodies against 33 ALS-associated proteins to identify high-quality reagents for use in western blot, immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. Using these antibodies, we profiled protein levels across human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary neurological cell types. These analyses revealed diverse cellular distributions and higher levels of several ALS-associated proteins in glial populations, consistent with emerging evidence for immune contributions to ALS. Together, ALS-RAP provides a validated antibody toolbox and protein expression resource to support the study of ALS-associated proteins.

abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor-odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a 'trunk-branch' network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR-Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

abstract: Tumorigenesis typically follows a multi-hit trajectory, driven by accumulating oncogenic mutations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) has long served as a paradigmatic model of multi-hit tumorigenesis, characterized by adenoma-carcinoma transition accompanied by acquisition of specific oncogene and tumor suppressor mutations. However, how the temporal order of early mutations influences CRC initiation remains poorly understood. To address this, we established a CRC tumorigenesis model using murine intestinal organoids. By introducing defined combinations of key CRC driver mutations ( Kras , Apc , and Trp53 ) in distinct orders, we systematically investigated how the order of mutation accumulation affects tumor initiation. Our results reveal that the mutation accumulation confers growth advantages in both in vitro and in vivo models. Strikingly, mutation order also influenced the tumorigenic properties of the organoids. Whereas organoids with Trp53 loss before or after Apc loss similarly affected organoid phenotypes in vitro or tumorigenicity in immunodeficient mice, organoids with Trp53 loss preceding Apc inactivation exhibited reduced tumor-forming potential in immunocompetent mice, likely due to their distinct immunological features. Collectively, our study reveals a critical role of ordered mutation accumulation in CRC initiation, an insight that may hold clinical relevance.

abstract: Adapting crops to intensive cultivation systems under climate change requires varieties that combine yield potential with optimized flowering and maturation . In central and eastern China, barley has long been cultivated in a double-season cropping system, in which early flowering and maturation are critical for escaping presummer terminal heat stress and enabling flexible rotation with summer crops . Here we trace the genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China using 505 representative cultivars and identify a flowering-time module defined by a single amino acid substitution in PHYTOCHROME C in combination with a winter-type VERNALIZATION 1 haplotype that underpins this adaptation. The derived allele accelerates heading and maturity, and its frequency has risen sharply in modern autumn-sown varieties. Using base editing in barley and wheat, we confirm causality and demonstrate that this flowering-time combination module, PhyC – VRN1 , is functionally conserved across Triticeae. Our results identify and experimentally validate a breeding-relevant flowering-time module that has been selected during modern breeding to enable intensive crop rotations, as well as demonstrate how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct such adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

author_details.affiliation: Wellcome Sanger Institute, Cambridge, UK; UCL Cancer Institute, University College London, London, UK

abstract: Cancer cells show highly heterogeneous and plastic states in glioblastoma, an incurable brain tumour . However, how these malignant states arise and whether they follow defined cellular trajectories across tumours is poorly understood. Here we generated a deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma that pairs transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling of 12 tumours across many regions. We identify that glioblastoma heterogeneity is driven by spatially patterned transitions of cancer cells from developmental-like states towards those defined by a glial injury response and hypoxia. This cellular trajectory regionalizes tumours into distinct tissue microenvironments and manifests in a molecularly conserved manner across tumours as well as genetically distinct tumour subclones. Consistently, using a new deep-learning framework to map cancer cell states jointly with clones in situ, we show that tumour subclones are finely spatially intermixed through glioblastoma tissue microenvironments. We validate this cellular trajectory by using somatic mutation-based hierarchies in vivo and an experimental patient-derived organoid model ex vivo. Finally, we show that this cancer cell trajectory is intimately linked to myeloid heterogeneity and unfolds across regionalized myeloid signalling environments. Our findings define a stereotyped trajectory of cancer cells in glioblastoma and unify glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity into a tractable cellular and tissue framework.

abstract: Inspired by macroscopic weaving techniques , molecular weaving, which interlaces molecular strands into ordered networks, has emerged as a powerful strategy for designing functional materials with emergent properties . However, so far, molecular weaving has relied mainly on linear building blocks and biaxial structures. Higher-order weaving (≥3 axes) of nonlinear building blocks is expected to produce intriguing architectures and bring new and unforeseen functions to the resulting materials; however, their construction and property investigation remain underexplored. Here we report a two-dimensional reticular triaxial woven polymer network constructed by incorporating C 3 -symmetric macrocycles into the woven structure through dative B–N polymerization. The resulting material not only exhibits unique topological chirality and robust mechanical properties but it also serves as a porous material that permits the separation of representative aromatic/aliphatic compounds. This functional utility highlights how higher-order triaxial woven topologies can provide unique advantages in terms of regulating material properties and introduces an extra topological dimension for the construction of functional materials.

abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III–V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance ( R S ) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

abstract: The ability to observe the social behaviour of others and use observed information to bias future action is a fundamental building block of social cognition . Aggression observation activates hypothalamic neurons relevant for aggression control , but whether observation and experience engage common circuit mechanisms that promote a new shared behavioural policy is unclear. Here we develop a strategy to perform large-scale cell-type-specific recordings across subcortical networks for social behaviour generation and learning. We record longitudinally while animals train through direct aggression experience or observation, then probe shared differences in behaviour and neural activity in a novel aggression context. After training, we detect unique signatures of a shared adaptive behavioural strategy that is absent in animals without training. During aggression observation, observed behaviour recruits widespread activation across subcortical networks for behavioural generation and mimics activity evoked by experienced behaviour, and shared neural changes persist into the novel aggression context. Multiregion modelling reveals shared changes to a core aggression network across both experience and observation, including a widespread reduction in inhibition, which we find is necessary for adaptive behavioural change. Together, this demonstrates that experience-like activity during aggression observation can recruit a shared inhibitory plasticity mechanism that biases behaviour toward adaptive proactive behavioural strategies.

abstract: Developing artificial intelligence (AI)-native experimental laboratories for autonomous scientific exploration with minimal human intervention represents a long-standing goal. Although autonomous experimental systems are emerging , especially in chemical and materials science, they remain largely confined to domains with singular objectives, well-defined workflows and simple instrumentation. This limitation may reflect an ‘add-on’ architecture that uses AI as a task-specific tool rather than providing it with a global understanding of experiments, especially under engineering-oriented circumstances. Here we present AutoDNA, an AI-native autonomous biomolecular engineering laboratory targeting multi-objective experiments across diverse instruments. Through the co-design of models, experiments and instruments, AutoDNA realizes the co-evolution of AI and the automation system within an end-to-end multi-user framework. The system autonomously orchestrates over 20 types of instruments across more than 11,000 steps to execute core nucleic acid operations including synthesis, transcription, amplification and sequencing, while human intervention is limited to hardware maintenance tasks, such as reagent and labware replenishment. Across four representative applications, AutoDNA matched expert-optimized enzymatic DNA synthesis yields, accelerated concurrent protocol execution by 3.2-fold, completed an end-to-end DNA data storage cycle with exact recovery of the original digital content, and identified and validated a clinically detected KRAS G13D mutation. AutoDNA establishes a blueprint towards science-as-a-service, accelerating biological discovery and advancing various applications in synthetic biology and information storage.

abstract: RNA language models have achieved strong performance across diverse downstream tasks by leveraging large-scale sequence data. However, RNA function is fundamentally shaped by hierarchical structure, making structural information important for pre-training. Existing approaches often depend on noisy annotations or task-specific objectives that can limit generalizability. Here we present structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model trained on 21 million RNA sequence–structure pairs by integrating base-pairing interactions into masked language modelling through a pair-matching operation. We also introduce MUSES, a multi-source ensemble of secondary structures designed to mitigate predictor bias, and a dynamic masking ratio that balances structure-guided and nucleotide-level masking. structRFM learns joint sequence and structure representations as sequence-level, nucleotide-level and pairwise features for broad downstream adaptation. It ranks highly in zero-shot homology classification and establishes new benchmarks for secondary-structure prediction. Its tertiary-structure adaptation, Zfold, consistently improves both three-dimensional predictions and their extracted secondary structures, with performance comparable to AlphaFold3 across CASP15-natural, CASP16 and RNA-Puzzles. structRFM also improves performance on function-prediction tasks and generalizes to newly released RNA families and long non-coding RNAs. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of structure-guided pre-training and highlight multimodal RNA language models for robust structural and functional inference. The complete 21-million-pair dataset, model weights and source code are openly available to support multimodal RNA foundation-model development.

abstract: Ribosomal frameshifting, an uncommon translational recoding event, is best known for its regulatory roles in viral gene expression , whereas its physiological relevance in mammals remains poorly understood. Here we show that specific codon pairs trigger efficient −1 frameshifting preferentially in cancer cells. Mechanistically, this recoding arises from ribosomal pausing associated with tRNA and amino acid availability, and is amplified by impaired ribosome quality control and sustained phosphorylation of ribosomal protein S6. We found that this codon-pair-specific frameshifting represents an intrinsic state of translational dysregulation, which is prevalent across cancer cells and reshapes protein synthesis. Taking advantage of this frameshifting-permissive state in cancer cells, we engineered a frameshifting-activated synthetic therapeutic circuit (FAST) that conditionally expresses the pyroptotic effector gasdermin D. FAST is activated across diverse cancer cell types, inducing potent and selective pyroptosis, while sparing normal tissues from detectable toxicity. As a proof of concept, systemic AAV9-mediated delivery of FAST in mouse models of colorectal and pancreatic cancer elicited pronounced tumour regression, robust immune activation and synergistic effects with immune checkpoint blockade. Collectively, these findings reveal codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting as a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells and establish translation-coupled gene circuits as a strategy for cancer-selective therapy.

abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events 1,2 . In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character 3,4 . Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world’s deadliest pathogen . Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations . Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis . These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein–protein interaction predictions for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

abstract: Perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells on rough textured substrates are at present limited by a critical trade-off in self-assembled monolayer (SAM) design because increasing molecular conjugation enhances conductivity but often leads to unfavourable aggregation that impairs conformal coverage . Here we overcome this challenge using a rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation that incorporates tailored intramolecular distortion to suppress excess π–π stacking without sacrificing charge-transport efficiency. This steric regulation facilitates the formation of a highly ordered, conformal SAM across rough pyramidal textures. By reconciling molecular packing with interfacial coverage, the tailored interface provides optimized energy-level alignment for ultrafast charge extraction, enables improved defect passivation through adaptive conformational adjustment and acts as a robust template for high-quality perovskite film growth. Making use of this interface, the optimized tandem device achieves a notable fill factor (FF) of 85%, yielding a certified stabilized power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 35.1%. Furthermore, the device demonstrates outstanding stability, retaining more than 94% of its initial performance after 1,500 h of ageing under the ISOS-L-1 protocol. Our findings provide a clear molecular engineering route to reconcile conductivity and film uniformity while maximizing the performance of tandem photovoltaics on textured silicon substrates.

abstract: Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

abstract: Mating decisions are often attributed to the sensory signalling between prospective sexual partners. Yet these interactions are also shaped by the broader environmental context in which they unfold, to appropriately align sexual arousal with reproductive opportunities . Here we show that in Drosophila erecta mating is strictly contingent on the ecological and social environment generated as flies densely aggregate in groups on a food patch. We find that food volatiles directly promote male sexual arousal, triggering individuals to sample and pursue potential mates, giving rise to dynamic interactions across the group. The ensuing visual motion transforms each male’s visual field, which in turn further amplifies his arousal, generating a multisensory feedback loop that coordinately promotes courtship across individuals. D. erecta ’s strict dependence on environmental cues appears latent in related species, such as Drosophila melanogaster , where food odour can promote arousal but is dispensable for vigorous courtship. Comparative circuit analyses show that species-specific thresholds for sexual arousal reflect variation in how olfactory input modulates conserved nodes controlling courtship drive, rendering food volatiles a strict sensory gate only in D. erecta . Together, our findings highlight how environmental cues not directly tied to sexual signalling can profoundly influence reproductive behaviour and reorganize the social landscape to ensure mating occurs in contexts where reproductive opportunities are abundant.

abstract: Sub-ångström spatial resolution combined with attosecond temporal resolution enables direct observation of electron motion in matter . Attosecond hard X-ray pulses generated at X-ray free-electron laser sources provide the requisite spatiotemporal sensitivity, yet their application has been limited by the absence of precise pulse metrology and control. Here, building on a broadband X-ray split-delay line, we establish metrology of attosecond hard X-ray pulses. Field-correlation measurements provide the first time-domain characterization of the pulse coherence time and demonstrate attosecond synchronization between the generated pulse pairs. By exploiting non-sequential two-photon absorption as a nonlinear probe, intensity autocorrelation quantifies the average pulse duration directly in the time domain to be 170 as. The demonstrated experimental tools and techniques enable systematic attosecond time-resolved experiments, including X-ray pump–X-ray probe spectroscopy and diffraction, and open a pathway to probing electronic phenomena with unprecedented spatial-temporal resolution.

abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au (ref. ) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation , effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation . Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation . Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories . Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2–15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. ) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed the treatment of haematological malignancies, but its efficacy remains limited by multiple negative regulatory mechanisms intrinsic to T cells . Here we perform a high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout (DKO) CRISPR screen, and identify multiple DKO gene pairs that are both effective and synergistic. The top pair, NR4A1 – SOCS3 DKO, has multiple favourable immunological features. Whole-transcriptome profiling and in vivo single-cell RNA sequencing reveal that NR4A1 – SOCS3 DKO specifically upregulates metabolic pathways in CAR-T cells, which show significantly higher metabolic fitness and mitochondrial activity. NR4A1 – SOCS3 DKO CAR-T cells and T cells exhibit exceptionally potent antitumour efficacy and long-term tumour control across different tumour models without compromising safety features. NR4A1 – SOCS3 DKO outperforms several benchmark single-gene and dual-gene modifications in T cells and CAR-T cells . These data demonstrate high-throughput in vivo CAR-T DKO screening for rapid discovery of combination targets, and establish NR4A1 – SOCS3 as a promising pair of intracellular checkpoints to engineer high-performance CAR-T therapies against cancer.

abstract: Alterations in the microbial composition of the human gut have been associated with a wide range of chronic diseases . Yet species-level composition alone can obscure extensive within-species genetic diversity and functional variation. This has driven a shift towards strain-resolved, genetic-level analysis of the microbiome, leveraging microbial genetic variation to identify disease-relevant genes and pathways . Here we conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) analysing 12.8 million gut microbial single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) with 244 host health phenotypes and environmental exposures in 10,781 individuals from 6 independent cohorts. We identify 940 independent associations across 69 host factors, including age, sex and cardiovascular and metabolic parameters. Structural analyses identified host-phenotype-associated SNVs in functionally important regions of proteins, findings that inform mechanistic hypotheses about how microbial genetic changes relate to environmental and host physiological factors. For example, we identified an age-associated SNV in Faecalibacterium prausnitzii that affects an amino acid within the protein pocket that binds glutathione. To support future efforts, all study summary statistics are provided in an online catalogue ( https://fulab.web.rug.nl/SNV-MWAS/ ). Together, these results identify new biological connections between the human host and microbial genetic variants at base pair resolution and provide a resource for hypothesis generation that will aid future understanding of the strain-level functionality of the gut microbiota.

abstract: Fibrous materials, ranging from connective tissues to engineered composites , are vital to many biological and man-made systems, optimized to withstand complex in operando or in vivo loading. The load-bearing capacity of intervertebral discs (IVDs) of the spine depends on a hierarchical extracellular matrix, where plywood-like lamellae of collagen fibres in the annulus fibrosus contain nanometre-scale fibrils built from staggered triple-helical monomers . How intact IVDs couple fibril-scale mechanics to fibre-scale organization under load remains unresolved. Here we introduce TomoSAXS, a full-field 3D small-angle X-ray scattering tomography that maps fibril-to-fibre mechanics across an intact tissue. We show that intrafibrillar molecular pre-strain (D-period stagger) is lamellar textured and tightly correlated with microscale fibre strain. Pre-strain is inversely related to fibril strain and its variability, consistent with load-sharing through molecular unwinding. Radial strain bridges and high-curvature zones at the annulus fibrosus–nucleus pulposus interfaces emerge as critical regulators of local mechanics. These findings reveal concerted fibril–fibre interactions that sustain mechanical equilibrium in the IVD, preserving elasticity and shape. More broadly, TomoSAXS establishes a platform to visualize nanoscale-to-microscale matrix mechanics across biological and synthetic fibrous materials, with applications in ageing and disease, therapeutic evaluation and the design of bio-based and bio-inspired materials.

abstract: Rubella virus (RuV) causes rubella and, when acquired during pregnancy, congenital rubella syndrome . Despite its clinical significance, the cellular entry mechanism of RuV remains poorly characterized, owing to limited identification of host receptors , which hinders pathogenesis research and therapeutic development. Here, using proximity biotin labelling-based proteomics coupled with CRISPR–Cas9 validation, we identify nectin-4 as a functional RuV entry receptor. Ectopic expression of nectin-4 conferred susceptibility to RuV in non-permissive cells, whereas blocking or genetic ablation of nectin-4 reduced infection, results that demonstrate that nectin-4 is a major entry factor. Mechanistically, nectin-4 directly interacts with the RuV envelope glycoprotein heterodimer and facilitates receptor-mediated endocytosis following initial calcium-dependent viral attachment to cellular lipids. In polarized airway epithelial models, nectin-4 mediates basolateral entry of RuV and supports apical progeny release, a finding that provides a molecular mechanism for respiratory transmission. In placental models, nectin-4 is highly expressed on syncytiotrophoblasts and facilitates infection at the maternal–fetal interface, although additional nectin-4-independent pathways contribute to infection of other trophoblast populations. Together, these data establish nectin-4 as a key factor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of RuV and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for the prevention of rubella and related diseases.

abstract: The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry . Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics—which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering —is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems . Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects , and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius–Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.

abstract: Algal bloom demise, often caused by viruses, is a major driver of carbon cycling in the surface ocean . However, although blooms collapse synchronously, fewer than 30% of algal cells are actively infected by viruses , indicating the involvement of additional mortality agents. Here we quantified tripartite interactions within a synthetic community composed of the abundant coccolithophore Gephyrocapsa huxleyi , bacteria and viruses isolated during a bloom. We found that bacteria significantly enhanced virus-induced algal mortality in G. huxleyi as well as in three other globally widespread microalgae. We quantified this interaction using two new metrics: the synergy index, which measures viral–bacterial interaction strength, and the benefit index, which assesses changes in bacterial fitness. We identified Alteromonas bacteria as drivers of viral–bacterial co-infection, with consistently high synergy index and benefit index. We found that during algal blooms, Alteromonas displayed high chemoattraction towards infected cell extracts, accumulated in aggregates derived from bloom demise, and increased in abundance during oceanic bloom collapse. Viral–bacterial synergy represents a previously unrecognized mortality agent that controls bloom termination, modulating the balance between the carbon-recycling viral shunt and the carbon-exporting viral shuttle pathways, which influence global carbon cycling .

abstract: The Great Unconformity marks a globally extensive erosive surface linked to climatic shifts and environmental transitions that preceded the Cambrian explosion of life. The processes proposed to explain the formation of the Great Unconformity include glacial erosion during the Snowball Earth , rifting and plume activity , sea-level fall and mantle-driven dynamic topography . However, the dynamics of these processes have not been tested. Here we show that continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity. Our models predict prolonged continental-scale Neoproterozoic uplift and long-term Phanerozoic subsidence for Laurentia, Baltica and North China. This vertical motion scenario is ideal for the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity, which is a first-order surface expression of deep Earth processes. The predicted prolonged continental uplift throughout Cryogenian times would have resulted in marked erosion due to the action of glaciers . The large area of Laurentia and limited deformation at its margins explain why the Great Unconformity is best preserved and documented there. Our models predict cycles of dynamic topography that are broadly reflected in preserved sediment volume across continents , and open new avenues for understanding the environments of Cambrian animal diversification.

abstract: Animals learn about the external world in part through interoceptive signals . For example, the nutrient content of food is first estimated in the mouth, in the form of flavour, and then it is measured again through slower signals from the gut. How these signals from the mouth and gut are integrated to drive learning is unclear. Here we identify a dopamine (DA) pathway that enables learning about the nutrient content of food. We show that DA neurons in the ventral tegmental area are necessary for associating nutrients with flavours, and that post-ingestive nutrients trigger DA release selectively in a small region of the anterior basolateral amygdala (BLA) but not in canonical DA targets in striatum. This nutrient-triggered DA release occurs preferentially in the left BLA in mice, and this same structure is preferentially activated by post-ingestive nutrients in humans. We identify the gut sensors that are responsible for nutrient-triggered DA release; show that they activate BLA-projecting DA neurons defined by expression of cholecystokinin; and demonstrate that stimulation of DA axon terminals in the anterior BLA drives flavour–nutrient learning but not other aspects of feeding behaviour. Two-photon imaging of neurons in the left anterior BLA reveals that they integrate gustatory and post-ingestive cues, and silencing these neurons prevents flavour–nutrient learning. These findings establish a neural basis for how animals learn about the nutrient content of their food.

abstract: Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies , but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale . This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction . Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 bp (calibrated years before present or 1950 ce ) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800–3200 bp ), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz–Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200–2800 bp ), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts . Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD . Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge . Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals , and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts ; however, the biological basis of this ‘female protective effect’ (FPE) has remained unknown . Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST . Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals , emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

abstract: Two-dimensional semiconducting moiré superlattices provide a highly tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated and topological quantum phases . As a prototypical example, twisted bilayer MoTe 2 (tMoTe 2 ) has been shown to host fractional topological phases at zero magnetic field . However, their evolution with twist angle and competition with other correlated quantum states remain largely unexplored. Here we report a systematic transport study of twist-angle-dependent phase diagrams in tMoTe 2 across a range of 3.79°–5.76°, revealing an evolution from valley-polarized, fractional topological states to valley-degenerate correlated states and superconductivity. At relatively small twist angles, partially filled Chern bands of tMoTe 2 host fractional quantum anomalous Hall states following the Jain sequence, together with signatures of an anomalous composite Fermi liquid at moiré hole filling factor ν h = 1/2. Increasing twist angle progressively suppresses fractional topological phases and reconstructs the half-filled Chern band into symmetry-breaking integer Chern insulating states. At ν h = 1, we observe a transition from robust integer quantum anomalous Hall insulators at small angles to displacement-field-tuned, topologically trivial correlated insulators at larger angles. At twist angles above approximately 5.6°, superconductivity emerges adjacent to the ν h = 1 correlated insulator, with a phase diagram closely resembling that recently reported in twisted bilayer WSe 2 (refs. ). Our results indicate a unified twist-angle-driven phase evolution linking fractional topology, symmetry breaking, magnetic order and superconductivity, providing new insight into the emergent quantum phenomena in moiré systems.
