title: The behaviour bends, the code holds: working-memory category information in the multiple-demand network across graded interruption
abstract: Protecting working memory (WM) from interference is essential for goal-directed behaviour, yet its neural mechanisms remain unclear. The multiple-demand (MD) network - a set of frontoparietal regions recruited by diverse cognitive demands - is a candidate system for maintaining WM content under interference. We examined how the MD network represents a memorandum when an unrelated task interrupts maintenance. Participants memorised an image of a tool or animal and, during the delay, performed a digit task whose difficulty was parametrically varied (passive, easy, hard), allowing us to test how task engagement and associated cognitive demands affected concurrently maintained information. Using fMRI and multivariate pattern analysis, we decoded the maintained category (tool vs. animal) from 13 MD regions and early visual cortex. Behaviourally, interruption reduced recall accuracy, while the most demanding interrupter slowed responses. Neurally, category information was present during the delay, most strongly in visual cortex and bilateral intraparietal sulcus. This information was unaffected by task engagement (active vs. passive), consistently across decoding accuracy and cross-validated Mahalanobis (crossnobis) distance, with Bayesian evidence supporting the null effect. Increasing the demand of the active interrupter, however, produced a modest, network-wide reduction in crossnobis distance that was not detectable in decoding accuracy. Together, these findings reveal a dissociation between the behavioural costs of interruption and the neural representation of maintained category information. Although interruption impaired recall, engaging in an interrupter did not measurably alter category-level information in the MD network or visual cortex. Increasing the demand of the interrupter produced only a modest, network-wide reduction in representational distance, without affecting decoding accuracy, suggesting that the behavioural costs of interruption may not be fully explained by changes in the categorical representation of the memorandum.
author_corresponding_institution: San Jose State University, University of Reading

title: The ontogeny of hippocampal spatial memory is supported by postnatal Cajal-Retzius cells
abstract: The functional capabilities of the adult hippocampus depend on specialized circuits that are established during development. Cajal-Retzius (CR) cells persist in the hippocampus long after their disappearance from the neocortex and contribute to the postnatal maturation of hippocampal circuits, but how this developmental role shapes adult hippocampal function remains unknown. Here, we selectively ablated CR cells from the postnatal hippocampus and examined the consequences for spatial learning, navigation, and CA1 spatial representations. CR-cell ablated animals learned reward locations and adapted to changing task conditions, but learned more slowly and made more errors. Reinforcement-learning models suggest that these behavioral differences reflect less stable internal representations guiding behavior. Consistent with this, CA1 spatial representations remained present but were more unstable and showed reduced differentiation of reward locations, particularly when task conditions changed. Our findings identify postnatal CR cells as key developmental contributors to the stability of hippocampal spatial representations and the adaptive behavior they support.

title: Unilateral naris occlusion with custom-made plugs for reversible olfactory deprivation in juvenile and adult mice
abstract: Deprivation paradigms that reduce environmental input have been successfully applied across multiple species and sensory modalities, including vision, audition, somatosensation, and olfaction in order to understand how neurons and circuits respond to loss of sensory input. One notable advantage of studying sensory deprivation in the rodent olfactory system is the ease and control with which smell loss can be induced. Various methods of olfactory deprivation have long been available and rely on blocking a nostril, either through invasive and often non-reversible approaches such as chemical ablation or surgical procedures, or through reversible approaches such as unilateral naris occlusion using custom-made nose plugs. Here, we provide a systematic description of this well-established method, including its construction from commercially available materials, procedures, validation, and reliability in post-weaning mice, thereby providing a detailed and reproducible framework for controlled, reversible olfactory deprivation.

title: Vision-language representations link food perception to subjective valuation
abstract: Subjective values of foods guide dietary decisions. Yet, how the brain computes such values from visual input remains unclear. Here, we show that visual food valuation relies on higher-level conceptual representations captured by a multimodal vision-language deep neural network model. Using food images and human ratings (N = 194 and 200), we found that a vision-language model predicted subjective value more accurately than vision-only models. Representational analyses demonstrated that, compared with the vision-only model, the vision-language model preferentially encoded higher-level food attributes, including perceived healthiness, while encoding less image-level visual information. Multivariate analyses of fMRI data (N = 31) showed that embedding features from both models corresponded to activity patterns along the visual pathways. Critically, vision-language features showed greater correspondence than vision-only features in the fusiform gyrus, a downstream region of the ventral visual pathway. These findings suggest that higher-level conceptual representations link visual food processing to subjective valuation.

abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO 2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level) 1 , significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition 1,2 . This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events 3,4 . Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

abstract: Atypical chemokine receptors (ACKRs) are non-signaling GPCRs that regulate ligand availability, with ACKR3 functioning as a dual scavenger of chemokines and opioid peptides. Here, we demonstrate that following ligand stimulation, besides the canonical internalization, ACKR3 is released on extracellular vesicles (EVs). ACKR3 was also found on EVs released under basal conditions, although to a lesser extent. These observations were confirmed across multiple cellular contexts, including endogenous systems. Mechanistically, basal and ligand-induced EV release are independent of GRKs and β-arrestin but each relies on different trafficking routes and C-terminal determinants. Ligand-induced EV release is associated with plasma membrane localization and receptor recycling pathways. In contrast, basal EV release is governed by intracellular sorting processes and influenced by receptor ubiquitination and RAMP3. Functionally, EV-associated ACKR3 retains high-affinity ligand binding, enabling sequestration of CXCL12 and opioid peptides and thereby attenuating their signaling through CXCR4 and MOR. We also show that the release on EVs, in particular under basal conditions, is observed for other receptors such as KOR, CXCR4 and several ACKRs. Collectively, these findings establish EVs as regulators in chemokine and opioid systems and as a distinct dimension of ACKR3 and more broadly GPCR biology.

abstract: Lipid metabolism is fundamental to cellular homeostasis, supporting energy storage, membrane architecture, and cellular signaling. Beyond these canonical roles, lipids have emerged as critical regulators of host immunity. Here, we define a lipid-driven mechanism that governs host–pathogen interactions by impacting pathogen clearance and thus infection outcomes. Exploiting Drosophila , we show that enteric infection triggers robust accumulation of neutral lipids, and specifically 1,2-diacylglycerols (DAGs), in the midgut. Disruption of DAG biosynthesis or lipid transport in midgut enterocytes (ECs) impairs lipid accumulation and reduces host survival. Conversely, dietary lipid supplementation enhances lipid storage and improves survival. Mechanistically, these lipid-dependent responses regulate defecation, thereby controlling bacterial clearance from the midgut. DAGs can act as signaling lipids that activate protein kinase C (PKC), and DAG accumulation in ECs correlates with elevated PKC activity and calcium signaling in midgut visceral muscle (VM), promoting VM contraction, midgut motility, and expulsion of pathogens via defecation. Together, our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for DAG metabolism in shaping host defenses.

abstract: Semantic processing relies on flexible interactions between specialized lexico-semantic regions and domain-general control networks, particularly under challenging conditions. Using transcranial magnetic stimulation interleaved with functional magnetic resonance imaging, we investigated acute network adaptation when the left posterior middle temporal gyrus—a core lexico-semantic region—was perturbed during lexico-semantic decisions in 25 healthy participants. High-intensity transcranial magnetic stimulation over the posterior middle temporal gyrus induced task-specific activity increases across semantic control and lexical retrieval areas, as well as remote domain-general regions. Critically, increased local activity at the stimulation site correlated with slower reaction times, whereas greater upregulation in domain-general frontal regions was associated with less disrupted semantic performance. These findings indicate that acute semantic disruption triggers immediate, flexible recruitment of domain-general control areas consistent with the maintenance of task performance, highlighting the brain’s capacity to dynamically adapt to interference. Our findings contribute to the current understanding of putative compensatory network-level mechanisms supporting lexico-semantic cognition.

abstract: The brain’s representations are encoded in the collective activity of neural populations whose non-monotonic tuning properties define the population code. Adaptive behavior calls for flexible retuning of this code as stimulus statistics change across contexts. Yet how such adaptation occurs is unknown. Using fMRI during a numerosity-estimation task with variable number ranges, we show that number representations in human parietal cortex dynamically recalibrate to context, enabling context-sensitive behavioral accuracy. The tuning properties of neural populations collectively shift and rescale with the range. This distributed range adaptation achieves efficient coding in real time: neural precision scales with the range and predicts corresponding changes in behavioral precision. Individuals with stronger neural adaptation show larger behavioral adjustments. These findings extend static sensory efficient coding to adaptive representations of abstract magnitudes. Such flexible population tuning may constitute a canonical mechanism of encoding networks that enables the brain to sustain precise, adaptive behavior.

abstract: Quantifying enzyme kinetic parameter changes upon mutations is essential for accelerating enzyme evolution. Current methods focus on predicting absolute values of kinetic parameters (turnover numbers k cat and Michaelis constants K m ), yet they fail to accurately capture mutation effects. To our knowledge, no method directly models mutation effects (Δ k cat and Δ K m ) due to the scarcity of such training data. Moreover, these methods haven’t fully exploited protein structural geometry. Here, we establish a high-quality enzyme mutation effect dataset by pairing wild-type and mutant kinetic parameters measured under identical experimental conditions via a semi-automatic procedure combining language model-assisted parsing and manual verification. Leveraging this dataset, we develop DeltaCata, a Siamese geometric graph neural network to directly predict the changes in kinetic parameters induced by residue substitutions. DeltaCata demonstrates substantial performance improvements over existing methods, especially for enzymes unseen in the training sets. Its utility is further validated through in silico beneficial mutation screening experiments using deep mutational scanning datasets. Finally, we apply DeltaCata to engineer the methyltransferase sGmOMT2, achieving up to a 7.0-fold improvement in catalytic efficiency for in vitro icaritin synthesis. These results suggest the high potential of DeltaCata for industrial enzyme engineering.

abstract: Affinity maturation is an essential process in antibody engineering. Although powerful, it is iterative, time-consuming, and can result in trade-offs, where affinity is gained at the cost of important properties, such as specificity and stability. We present a scalable strategy, called LAffAb, that starts from a crystallographic structure of the antibody-antigen complex and introduces combinations of mutations to the antibody to optimize the energy of the complex. A combinatorial library comprising 7000 variants with up to nine mutations results in gains of up to 30-fold in affinity while co-optimizing stability. Surprisingly, the library does not converge on a single solution, instead favoring diverse variants with a high mutational load. Small-scale screening of 10 designs against a potential drug target improves affinity by an order-of-magnitude while maintaining high developability. We also apply LAffAb to improve the developability of a therapeutic antibody while maintaining affinity. We envision that LAffAb can be used to design stable, specific, and high-affinity binders and to improve our understanding of sequence, structure, and function relationships in antibodies.

abstract: Understanding the behaviors of contractile actomyosin systems requires precise spatiotemporal control of filamentous myosin activity. Here, we develop a tool for optical control of contractility by extending the MyLOV family of gearshifting motors to create engineered filamentous myosins that change velocity in response to blue light. We characterize these minifilaments using in vitro single-molecule tracking assays, contractility assays in reconstituted actin networks, and imaging of contractile phenotypes in live cells. In vitro, gearshifting minifilaments change speed and/or direction when illuminated, and contraction rates of minifilaments in actin networks can be modulated using blue light. In cells, gearshifting minifilaments enable optical control of protrusion retraction, cortical flow, and cell migration. Finally, we develop an alternative design for minifilaments that only interact processively with actin in blue light. Engineered minifilaments could be used to dissect behaviors such as self-organization and mechanotransduction in contractile systems both in vitro and in cells and tissues.

abstract: Bidirectional promoters (BDPs), intergenic regions that coordinate transcription of oppositely oriented genes, pervade eukaryotic genomes, yet sequence signatures remain poorly defined. Existing approaches to BDP identification rely on distance thresholds and cannot infer activity from DNA. Here, we use Evo2, a genomic language model, to predict BDP activity and uncover sequence-encoded regulatory principles across four plant species ( Arabidopsis , maize, rice, and wheat). We stratify BDPs by co-expression strength and compare Evo2-derived embeddings against k -mer profiles, transcription factor binding site matrices, and convolutional neural networks trained on sequence. Evo2 embeddings outperform all baselines, demonstrating that genomic language models capture regulatory information underlying BDP activity. Models trained on one or multiple species transfer to held-out species, and in planta validation in Spartina alterniflora confirms predicted high-activity BDPs. Sparse autoencoder analysis links Evo2 embeddings to nucleosome positioning and species-specific transcription factor landscapes, providing insight into sequence determinants underlying BDP activity . This work establishes how genomic language models can extract bidirectional promoter logic from sequence and identify conserved regulatory rules across plants.

abstract: Differentiating arginine vasopressin (AVP) deficiency from primary polydipsia is challenging. The most accurate test, hypertonic saline–stimulated copeptin, requires intensive monitoring. Intravenous mannitol stimulates AVP release and may provide a simpler alternative. In a randomized double-blind crossover trial, 22 healthy adults received mannitol and placebo in random order, of whom 21 were included in the primary analysis. In a pilot study, 10 patients with AVP deficiency and 10 with primary polydipsia received mannitol. The primary outcome was copeptin after mannitol infusion. Mannitol resulted in a 2.29-fold higher copeptin at 90 minutes (+6.4 pmol/L (95% CI: +5.2, +7.7; p <0.001)) than after placebo at mean baseline copeptin levels in healthy adults. In patients, copeptin after 30 minutes was 11.7 pmol/L (95% CI: 6.5, 17.0) higher in primary polydipsia than in AVP deficiency. Mannitol infusion shows promise as a new diagnostic approach. Larger confirmatory studies are required to validate both the optimal diagnostic cut-off and patient safety. Trial Registration number: NCT06542198 .

abstract: Effective stress coping relies on neural and endocrine coordination, with the mesostriatal system serving as a central substrate. However, how striatal subregions contribute to stress vulnerability versus resilience remains unclear. Here, we show dissociable roles of the nucleus accumbens (NAC) and dorsal caudate (dCA) and their associated brain networks in shaping stress responses. We identify neural stability (NS)—capturing stress-induced changes in state-switching frequency over the course of stress responses—as a marker: task-state NS correlates positively with stress-related NAC activity, whereas resting-state NS correlates inversely with stress-related dCA activity. NAC-mediated networks and associated NS further predict faster cortisol recovery. Intriguingly, NAC-related functional connectivity patterns spatially covary with dopamine D 2 receptor distributions and gene expression in inhibitory neurons and glia, whereas dCA-related patterns covary with μ-opioid receptor distributions. Together, these findings reveal striatal subregional heterogeneity in stress coping and characterize resilience as a multisystem homeostatic process integrating neural, endocrine, and molecular layers.

abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced bone loss (GIBL) remains a major clinical challenge, manifested by both systemic osteopenia and osteonecrosis of the femoral head under chronic glucocorticoid exposure, yet current therapies are limited in coordinately addressing bone deterioration and vascular impairment. With advances in precision medicine, oligonucleotide therapeutics offer opportunities for pathophysiology-informed intervention. Here, we report a pathology-adapted peptide-oligonucleotide nanohybrid (PON) developed for targeted miR-26a-5p delivery to glucocorticoid-injured bone. By integrating self-assembly, bone targeting, enzyme responsiveness, cell penetration, and lysosomal escape, PONs were designed to incorporate pathology-responsive delivery features and address key barriers to oligonucleotide delivery. Mechanistically, PON-mediated miR-26a-5p delivery reduced GSK-3β expression and promoted HIF-1α stabilization, thereby preserving osteogenesis-angiogenesis coupling and attenuating apoptosis. In a rat model of GIBL, systemic PON administration protects against early skeletal and vascular injury and limits progression after disease establishment. These findings identify the therapeutic relevance of miR-26a-5p in GIBL, and support the potential of PON system for bone-targeted oligonucleotide therapy.

abstract: Musculoskeletal infections (MSIs), including fracture-related infections (FRIs) and periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), remain difficult to treat because of biofilm formation and increasing antimicrobial resistance. Bacteriophage therapy (PT) has re-emerged as a promising adjunctive strategy, although prospective clinical evidence remains scarce. Here, we prospectively evaluated adjunctive local PT in 13 patients with refractory MSIs treated within the multidisciplinary PHAGEFORCE framework at University Hospitals Leuven (BE). Following surgery, personalized phage preparations were administered through a closed drain system for 8–10 days alongside systemic antibiotics. Clinical, microbiological, immunological, and genomic data were collected. Four patients with refractory MSIs lacking suitable phages served as a control cohort. Clinical remission was observed in nine of eleven evaluable phage-treated patients (82%), whereas all control patients experienced infection recurrence during follow-up. PT was well tolerated, with no serious adverse reactions or clinically meaningful toxicity. Local phage titers remained detectable throughout therapy despite interpatient variability. Serum-mediated phage neutralization was observed during and after PT, and longitudinal genomic monitoring revealed patient-specific phage dynamics, neither of which was clearly associated with clinical outcome. These findings demonstrate the feasibility and safety of standardized local PT and support further evaluation of this approach in controlled clinical trials.

abstract: Resident cardiac macrophages (RCM) are essential for myocardial repair following acute myocardial infarction (AMI); however, their therapeutic application is hindered by limited availability. Here, we show that RCM transplantation from healthy mice markedly attenuates cardiac injury in mice. Importantly, we identify a pro-reparative CD301b⁺ RCM population profoundly depleted after AMI and show that adoptive transfer of this subset alone mitigates cardiac injury following myocardial infarction. To overcome the scarcity of native RCMs and favour their replenishment, we expand ex vivo a CD301b + macrophage-like population (RCML) by polarizing bone marrow-derived macrophages with an ILC2-derived cytokine cocktail, and show that RCML transplantation confers robust post-AMI cardioprotection. Mechanistically, CD301b promotes efferocytosis by enhancing TFEB-mediated lysosomal function via a GATM-AMPK-mTOR axis, a pathway conserved in human macrophages. Thus, our findings identify a key pro-reparative macrophage subset and establish a feasible cell-based strategy for cardiac repair.

abstract: Non-human primates like rhesus macaques are pivotal models for decoding human visual cortex physiology and disorders. However, there is a lack of high-resolution transcriptomic atlases comparing distinct areas of the visual cortex in macaque. Here, we developed BrainSPACE, an innovative pipeline for rapid and precise brain tissue banking, to sample visual cortex areas: V1, V2, V4, MT, and TEO. We applied single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) to unravel neuronal diversity in BrainSPACE-banked V1 and V4 areas ( ~ 100,000 nuclei). We uncovered conserved GABAergic neuron profiles but stark area-specific diversity in principal neurons, featuring seven unique layer 4 subtypes in V1 and one in V4. Complementary smFISH validated transcriptional gradients across these areas, aligning with ventral and dorsal stream hierarchies. Gene ontology analyses highlighted plasticity-related pathways in unique layer 4 subtypes, with genes like NTNG1 and NLGN1 linked to neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism and schizophrenia. Our insights bridge molecular architecture to visual processing, offering an interactive atlas for community use. By revealing how layer 4 heterogeneity drives hierarchical specialization, our work advances primate brain mapping and informs therapeutic strategies for vision-related pathologies.

abstract: The modular architecture of multi-domain enzymes is a key source of functional diversity. GH18 chitinases exemplify this, possessing a variety of auxiliary domains that have been postulated to underpin their role as essential global nutrient cyclers. However, there is no evolutionary framework that accounts for the vast assortment of domain compositions observed across the protein family. Here, we map the sequence space of prokaryotic chitinases, integrating phylogenetics with a quantitative analysis of domain promiscuity to decode their evolutionary history. We reveal that diversification follows distinct trajectories: enzymes necessary for environmental chitin scavenging evolve via high modular plasticity and structural elaboration of the catalytic core, whereas sequences required for specialized, essential developmental roles fix their domain architecture to fulfil lineage-specific physiological roles. By resolving how domain accretion co-evolves with catalytic scaffolds, this work provides a framework for understanding how multi-domain enzymes adapt to complex environments.

abstract: Equine rhinitis A virus (ERAV), a picornavirus closely related to foot-and-mouth disease virus, causes respiratory infections in horses. We performed a HEK293T CRISPRi screen and identified integrin α2β1 as a protein receptor for ERAV. Using knock-out cells and pretreating cells with an antibody or soluble receptor, we confirmed the importance of this integrin for infection of multiple cell types, including equine fibroblasts. Cryo-EM and glycoproteomics analyses revealed that ERAV binds integrin α2β1 in its closed conformation by attaching to the β-propeller of the α2 chain, independent of divalent cations, as well as to a high-mannose glycan on α2 N112 and a sialylated glycan on β1 N269. Using glycan knockout and knock-in cells and by reconstituting integrin α2β1-depleted cells with mutant receptors, we demonstrated the importance of these glycans for virus entry. Our results identify a hitherto unseen combination of protein and glycan interactions between a virus and its receptor.

abstract: Autonomous sensors and machine learning are transforming ecology by enabling large-scale observation of organisms and ecosystems. However, camera traps, audio recorders and other sensors currently produce species-level detections. Tracking individuals continues to require invasive, high-effort capture–mark–recapture. Here we introduce an automated, general approach that identifies individual animals in passive acoustic recordings based on individually distinctive vocalizations. We train a convolutional neural network to extract salient features from audio recordings using a location-prediction task, then apply dimensionality reduction and clustering on features to achieve song-based individual identification. We identify individuals not included in the training data with 96% accuracy. We apply this approach to track 405 male ovenbirds ( Seiurus aurocapilla ) from 126 locations across 4 years, then model abundance and apparent survival. We provide open-source code to facilitate applications of our approach to other species. Performing automated individual identification on passive acoustic datasets will support the study of population trajectories and inform proactive ecosystem management to prevent biodiversity loss.

abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets. Across sequencing-based and imaging-based datasets, DIRAC identified a new microvascular proliferation domain in glioblastoma, corrected cortical-layer annotations in severe Alzheimer’s disease, resolved subtle structures in mouse embryos and remained robust to missing data and unseen cell types. We generated mouse spleen and thymus Stereo-CITE-seq data and used DIRAC to reveal thymic T cell migration and splenic immune cell interactions. DIRAC is fast and scales to millions of cells.

abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies have enhanced our understanding of diverse cellular identities, compositions, architectures and functions. However, the single-cell three-dimensional (3D) organization of the epigenome is still not well understood, due to an absence of spatial single-cell methods that allow high-resolution, locus-specific detection of combinations of epigenetic marks while maintaining 3D genome organization. Here we develop epigenetic proximity hybridization reaction (Epi-PHR), a nondisruptive image-based single-cell spatial epigenetic profiling technology. Epi-PHR detects combinations of epigenetic marks in situ at hundreds of gene targets within single cells while preserving 3D genome organization. Phased Epi-PHR combined with chromatin tracing reveals unexpected associations between epigenetic mark enrichment and chromatin folding of an imprinted gene cluster at the single-chromatin-copy level for the distinct alleles from different parental origins. We expect Epi-PHR will be broadly applicable in research requiring single-cell spatial epigenetic information, advancing our understanding of the combinatorial epigenetic code and its relationship with chromatin organization.

abstract: Understanding the subcellular localization of RNAs is critical for their functions, but visualizing circular RNAs (circRNAs) has been hindered by their sequence overlap with linear counterparts. Here we developed amplicon-based circRNA fluorescence in situ hybridization (abcFISH), which uses an optimized rolling-circle amplification strategy targeting back-splicing junction sites for robust, high specificity, single-molecule circRNA imaging. abcFISH enables quantitative, multiplexed imaging in cells and tissues, allowing us to reveal alternative circularization patterns from the single locus, uncover cell-type-specific circRNA expression linked to combinatorial effects of RNA-binding proteins, map distinct spatial distribution patterns of circRNAs in neurons and brain tissues, and show functional colocalization of circRNA Cdr1as and long noncoding RNA Cyrano. We further applied abcFISH to validate therapeutic double-stranded circRNA aptamers, simultaneously visualizing AAV-delivered double-stranded circRNA aptamers and the resulting reduction in astrocyte infiltration around transduced cells. Collectively, abcFISH provides a robust, user-friendly toolkit for deciphering circRNA localization and function in vivo.
